# Genesis

בראשית

Link: [https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis)

בריאת העולם, תחילתה של האנושות וסיפורי האבות והאמהות.

Creation, the beginning of mankind, and stories of the patriarchs and matriarchs.

Sections: Chapter-Verse

Location: Tanakh/Torah

Originally from [Sefaria](https://www.sefaria.org) via [TorahLM.org](https://torahlm.org) — see [licensing](https://torahlm.org/sefaria_license).

Version (He): Miqra according to the Masorah (Segments: 1533, License: CC-BY-SA)

Versions (En):
  - Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009 (Segments: 1533, License: CC-BY)
  - The Koren Jerusalem Bible (Segments: 1533, License: CC-BY-NC)
  - The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein (Segments: 1533, License: CC-BY)


## Chapter 1

###### Genesis 1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:1)


בְּרֵאשִׁ֖ית בָּרָ֣א אֱלֹהִ֑ים אֵ֥ת הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וְאֵ֥ת הָאָֽרֶץ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
In the beginning Elohim created the heavens and the earth.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
IN THE BEGINNING God created the heaven and the earth.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
In the beginning of the creation by G-d [Elokim, the attribute of justice,] of the heavens and the earth, [G-d first intending to create the world with the attribute of justice but then granting precedence to the attribute of mercy (Yod-Key-Vav-Key), seeing that the world could not otherwise endure],


###### Genesis 1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:2)


וְהָאָ֗רֶץ הָיְתָ֥ה תֹ֙הוּ֙ וָבֹ֔הוּ וְחֹ֖שֶׁךְ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י תְה֑וֹם וְר֣וּחַ אֱלֹהִ֔ים מְרַחֶ֖פֶת עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַמָּֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The earth was unformed and desolate, and (there was) darkness over the surface of the abyss. The breath of Elohim hovered above the surface of the water.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the earth was without form and void; and darkness was on the face of the deep. And a wind from God moved over the surface of the waters.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
the earth was vacuous and void, and there was darkness upon the face of the deep [i.e., the waters], and the "wind of G-d" [the Throne of Glory, impelled by His utterance] hovered over the face of the waters.


###### Genesis 1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:3)


וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֖ים יְהִ֣י א֑וֹר וַֽיְהִי־אֽוֹר׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Elohim said, Let there be light. and there was light.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And G-d said: Let there be light! And there was light.


###### Genesis 1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:4)


וַיַּ֧רְא אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת־הָא֖וֹר כִּי־ט֑וֹב וַיַּבְדֵּ֣ל אֱלֹהִ֔ים בֵּ֥ין הָא֖וֹר וּבֵ֥ין הַחֹֽשֶׁךְ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Elohim saw that the light was good, and Elohim divided the light from the darkness.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And God saw the light, that it was good: and God divided the light from the darkness.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And G-d saw that the light was good, [and that it was not appropriate for light and darkness to serve in combination] and G-d separated between the light and the darkness, [making the day the domain of the first and the night the domain of the second].


###### Genesis 1:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:5)


וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֱלֹהִ֤ים׀לָאוֹר֙ י֔וֹם וְלַחֹ֖שֶׁךְ קָ֣רָא לָ֑יְלָה וַֽיְהִי־עֶ֥רֶב וַֽיְהִי־בֹ֖קֶר י֥וֹם אֶחָֽד׃{פ}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Elohim called the light day, and the darkness He called night. It became evening and it became morning, one day.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And God called the light Day, and the darkness He called Night. And there was evening and there was morning, one day.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And G-d called the light day, and the darkness He called night. And it was evening and it was morning, the day of the One, [the angels not being created until the second day].


###### Genesis 1:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:6)


וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֔ים יְהִ֥י רָקִ֖יעַ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַמָּ֑יִם וִיהִ֣י מַבְדִּ֔יל בֵּ֥ין מַ֖יִם לָמָֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Elohim said, Let there be a canopy in the midst of the waters, and let it divide between waters and waters.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And God said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide water from water.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And G-d said: Let there be a firmament [i.e., let the firmament be hardened] in the midst of the waters, [the upper waters being at a distance from the firmament just as the lower waters are], and let it divide between waters and waters.


###### Genesis 1:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:7)


וַיַּ֣עַשׂ אֱלֹהִים֮ אֶת־הָרָקִ֒יעַ֒ וַיַּבְדֵּ֗ל בֵּ֤ין הַמַּ֙יִם֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ מִתַּ֣חַת לָרָקִ֔יעַ וּבֵ֣ין הַמַּ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֖ר מֵעַ֣ל לָרָקִ֑יעַ וַֽיְהִי־כֵֽן׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Elohim made the canopy, and divided the waters which were beneath the canopy, from the waters which were above the canopy, and it was so.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And God made the firmament, and divided the waters which were under the firmament from the waters which were above the firmament: and it was so.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And G-d made [i.e., fixed in place] the firmament, and He divided between the waters below the firmament and the waters above the firmament; and it was so.


###### Genesis 1:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:8)


וַיִּקְרָ֧א אֱלֹהִ֛ים לָֽרָקִ֖יעַ שָׁמָ֑יִם וַֽיְהִי־עֶ֥רֶב וַֽיְהִי־בֹ֖קֶר י֥וֹם שֵׁנִֽי׃{פ}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Elohim called the canopy heaven. It became evening and it became morning the second day.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And God called the firmament Heaven. And there was evening and there was morning, a second day.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And G-d called the firmament shamayim [sa mayim - it "carries" water (the upper waters); sham mayim - water is there; esh umayim - fire and water (the firmament being a combination of the two)]. And it was evening, and it was morning, the second day.


###### Genesis 1:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:9)


וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים יִקָּו֨וּ הַמַּ֜יִם מִתַּ֤חַת הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ אֶל־מָק֣וֹם אֶחָ֔ד וְתֵרָאֶ֖ה הַיַּבָּשָׁ֑ה וַֽיְהִי־כֵֽן׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Elohim said, Let the waters beneath the heavens be gathered into one place, and let the dryness be seen. It was so.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And God said, Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together to one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And G-d said: Let the waters below the heavens, [which were spread over the entire earth], be gathered into one place [the ocean], and let the dry land be seen; and it was so.


###### Genesis 1:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:10)


וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֱלֹהִ֤ים׀לַיַּבָּשָׁה֙ אֶ֔רֶץ וּלְמִקְוֵ֥ה הַמַּ֖יִם קָרָ֣א יַמִּ֑ים וַיַּ֥רְא אֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי־טֽוֹב׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Elohim called the dryness, earth, and the gathering of the waters, He called seas, and Elohim saw that it was good.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And God called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters He called Seas: and God saw that it was good.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And G-d called the dry land "earth," and the gathering of the waters He called "seas" [(plural, fish from different regions of the sea having distinctive tastes)], and G-d saw that it was good, [the "work of the waters" being completed on that day].


###### Genesis 1:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:11)


וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים תַּֽדְשֵׁ֤א הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ דֶּ֗שֶׁא עֵ֚שֶׂב מַזְרִ֣יעַ זֶ֔רַע עֵ֣ץ פְּרִ֞י עֹ֤שֶׂה פְּרִי֙ לְמִינ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר זַרְעוֹ־ב֖וֹ עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַֽיְהִי־כֵֽן׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Elohim said, Let the earth sprout grass, seed-yielding herbs, fruit trees bearing fruit of its own kind, with its seed within it, upon the earth. And it was so.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, herb yielding seed, and fruit tree yielding fruit after its kind, whose seed is in itself, upon the earth: and it was so.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And G-d said: Let the earth put forth [a blanket of] herbage, grass yielding seed, fruit-tree, [the tree tasting like the fruit], giving fruit of its kind, whose seed is in it [to grow a tree of the same kind] upon the earth; and it was so.


###### Genesis 1:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:12)


וַתּוֹצֵ֨א הָאָ֜רֶץ דֶּ֠שֶׁא עֵ֣שֶׂב מַזְרִ֤יעַ זֶ֙רַע֙ לְמִינֵ֔הוּ וְעֵ֧ץ עֹֽשֶׂה־פְּרִ֛י אֲשֶׁ֥ר זַרְעוֹ־ב֖וֹ לְמִינֵ֑הוּ וַיַּ֥רְא אֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי־טֽוֹב׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The earth brought forth grass, herbs yielding seed of its kind, and trees bearing fruit which has in it seeds of its kind; and Elohim saw that it was good.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the earth brought forth grass, herb yielding seed after its kind, and tree yielding fruit, whose seed was in itself, after its kind: and God saw that it was good.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the earth put forth herbage, grass yielding seed according to its kind [though not having been commanded to do so], and tree giving fruit [(but not "fruit-tree" as commanded (11), for which the earth was subsequently punished, together with Adam)], whose seed is in it according to its kind. And G-d saw that it was good.


###### Genesis 1:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:13)


וַֽיְהִי־עֶ֥רֶב וַֽיְהִי־בֹ֖קֶר י֥וֹם שְׁלִישִֽׁי׃{פ}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
It became evening and it became morning, the third day.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And there was evening and there was morning, a third day.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And it was evening, and it was morning, the third day.


###### Genesis 1:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:14)


וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים יְהִ֤י מְאֹרֹת֙ בִּרְקִ֣יעַ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם לְהַבְדִּ֕יל בֵּ֥ין הַיּ֖וֹם וּבֵ֣ין הַלָּ֑יְלָה וְהָי֤וּ לְאֹתֹת֙ וּלְמ֣וֹעֲדִ֔ים וּלְיָמִ֖ים וְשָׁנִֽים׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Elohim said, Let there be lights in the canopy of heaven to divide between the day and the night, and they will serve for signs for seasons, (for) days and (for) years.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And G-d said: Let there be [suspended] luminaries in the firmament of the heaven [(The luminaries, like all things pertaining to heaven and to earth, had been created on the first day, but each of the particular creations was activated on its particular day.)] to divide between the day and the night, [after the first light had been secreted for the righteous for the world to come.] And let them serve for signs [(eclipses being omens of ill)], and for festivals, [reckoned by the New Moon], and for days, [the sun and the moon serving for half a day respectively], and for years, [completing their course through the zodiac in 365 days].


###### Genesis 1:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:15)


וְהָי֤וּ לִמְאוֹרֹת֙ בִּרְקִ֣יעַ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם לְהָאִ֖יר עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַֽיְהִי־כֵֽן׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
They will be for lights in the canopy of heaven to illuminate the earth. And it was so.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and let them be for lights in the firmament of heaven to give light upon the earth: and it was so.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And let them [in addition] be luminaries in the firmament of the heaven to illuminate the earth; and it was so.


###### Genesis 1:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:16)


וַיַּ֣עַשׂ אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶת־שְׁנֵ֥י הַמְּאֹרֹ֖ת הַגְּדֹלִ֑ים אֶת־הַמָּא֤וֹר הַגָּדֹל֙ לְמֶמְשֶׁ֣לֶת הַיּ֔וֹם וְאֶת־הַמָּא֤וֹר הַקָּטֹן֙ לְמֶמְשֶׁ֣לֶת הַלַּ֔יְלָה וְאֵ֖ת הַכּוֹכָבִֽים׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Elohim made the two great lights, the large light to rule the day, and the small light to rule the night, and the stars


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And God made the two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: and the stars also.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And G-d made the two great luminaries [(They were created of equal size, but when the moon protested "two kings reigning with one crown," it was diminished)], the great luminary for governance of the day, and the small luminary for governance of the night, and the stars, [(G-d multiplying the moon's hosts to "appease" it for its diminution)].


###### Genesis 1:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:17)


וַיִּתֵּ֥ן אֹתָ֛ם אֱלֹהִ֖ים בִּרְקִ֣יעַ הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם לְהָאִ֖יר עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Elohim set them in the canopy of the heaven to illuminate the earth,


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And God set them in the firmament of heaven to give light upon the earth,


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And G-d set them in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth.


###### Genesis 1:18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:18)


וְלִמְשֹׁל֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם וּבַלַּ֔יְלָה וּֽלְהַבְדִּ֔יל בֵּ֥ין הָא֖וֹר וּבֵ֣ין הַחֹ֑שֶׁךְ וַיַּ֥רְא אֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי־טֽוֹב׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
to rule in the day and the night, and to divide between the light and the darkness; and Elohim saw that it was good.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness: and God saw that it was good.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And to rule by day and by night, and to divide between the light and the darkness. And G-d saw that it was good.


###### Genesis 1:19

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:19](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:19)


וַֽיְהִי־עֶ֥רֶב וַֽיְהִי־בֹ֖קֶר י֥וֹם רְבִיעִֽי׃{פ}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
It became evening and it became morning, the fourth day.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And there was evening and there was morning, a fourth day.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And it was evening, and it was morning, the fourth day.


###### Genesis 1:20

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:20](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:20)


וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֔ים יִשְׁרְצ֣וּ הַמַּ֔יִם שֶׁ֖רֶץ נֶ֣פֶשׁ חַיָּ֑ה וְעוֹף֙ יְעוֹפֵ֣ף עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ עַל־פְּנֵ֖י רְקִ֥יעַ הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Elohim said, Let the waters teem with swarms of living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth, in the open canopy of the heaven.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And God said, Let the waters swarm abundantly with moving creatures that have life, and let birds fly above the earth in the open firmament of heaven.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And G-d said: Let the waters swarm a swarming (sheretz) [creatures not higher than the ground (e.g., flies, worms, rodents, fish)] infused with life, and birds flying above the earth on the face of the firmament of heaven.


###### Genesis 1:21

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:21](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:21)


וַיִּבְרָ֣א אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶת־הַתַּנִּינִ֖ם הַגְּדֹלִ֑ים וְאֵ֣ת כׇּל־נֶ֣פֶשׁ הַֽחַיָּ֣ה׀הָֽרֹמֶ֡שֶׂת אֲשֶׁר֩ שָׁרְצ֨וּ הַמַּ֜יִם לְמִֽינֵהֶ֗ם וְאֵ֨ת כׇּל־ע֤וֹף כָּנָף֙ לְמִינֵ֔הוּ וַיַּ֥רְא אֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי־טֽוֹב׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
And thus Elohim created the great whales, and every living creature that creeps, with which the waters teem, of its kind, and every winged bird of its kind; and Elohim saw that it was good.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And God created the great crocodiles, and every living creature that moves, which the waters brought forth abundantly, after their kind, and every winged bird after its kind: and God saw that it was good.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And G-d created the leviathans and all the creeping life-infused creatures, swarmed by the waters according to their kinds, and every winged bird according to its kind, and G-d saw that it was good.


###### Genesis 1:22

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Elohim blessed them saying, Be fruitful and multiply, fill the waters of the seas, and let the birds multiply on the earth.

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

It became evening and it became morning, the fifth day.

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

###### Genesis 1:25

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And G-d said: Let us make man [(G-d in His humility "asking leave" of the angels)] in our image according to our likeness [to understand and to know], and yirdu [connoting "they shall have dominion over" (if they are virtuous) or (if they are not), "they shall be humbled before"] the fish of the sea, the birds of the heaven, the beasts, and all the earth, and all the creeping things that creep on the earth.

And thus Elohim created man in his image. In the form of Elohim, He created him, male and female, He created them.

And G-d created the man in his mould [that He had cast for him (Adam, as opposed to the other creations, being created by "hand" and not by pronouncement)]; in the image of G-d He created him; male and female He created them [on the sixth day, forming Eve from Adam's side].


###### Genesis 1:28

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:28](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/1:28)


וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֹתָם֮ אֱלֹהִים֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לָהֶ֜ם אֱלֹהִ֗ים פְּר֥וּ וּרְב֛וּ וּמִלְא֥וּ אֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ וְכִבְשֻׁ֑הָ וּרְד֞וּ בִּדְגַ֤ת הַיָּם֙ וּבְע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וּבְכׇל־חַיָּ֖ה הָֽרֹמֶ֥שֶׂת עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Elohim blessed them, and Elohim said to them, Be fruitful and multiply, fill the earth and subdue it, and dominate the fish of the sea, the birds of the heaven, and every living thing that moves upon the earth.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And God blessed them, and God said to them, Be fruitful, and multiply, replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the air, and over every living thing that moves on the earth.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And G-d blessed them, and G-d said to them: Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth and subdue it [(also readable as "subdue her," connoting both that the mitzvah of procreation is his and not hers, and that he is to keep her from being "free" with herself)], and have dominion over the fish of the sea and the birds of the heaven, and over all the animals that range the earth.

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

And G-d said: Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed upon the face of the earth and every tree which has in it fruit of a tree, bearing seed. To you shall it be for food, [man not being permitted to kill animals for food until after the flood].

## Chapter 2

###### Genesis 2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/2:1)


וַיְכֻלּ֛וּ הַשָּׁמַ֥יִם וְהָאָ֖רֶץ וְכׇל־צְבָאָֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The heavens and the earth were completed, and [so were] all their conglomerations.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all their host.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the heavens and the earth were finished, and all of their hosts.


###### Genesis 2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/2:2)


וַיְכַ֤ל אֱלֹהִים֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י מְלַאכְתּ֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה וַיִּשְׁבֹּת֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י מִכׇּל־מְלַאכְתּ֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Elohim completed by the seventh day His work which He had made, and He abstained on the seventh day from all His work which He had made.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And by the seventh day God ended His work which He had done; and He rested on the seventh day from all His work which He had done.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And G-d completed on [i.e., precisely upon the advent of] the seventh day His work that He had done, and He rested on the seventh day, from all the work that He had done.


###### Genesis 2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/2:3)


וַיְבָ֤רֶךְ אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־י֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י וַיְקַדֵּ֖שׁ אֹת֑וֹ כִּ֣י ב֤וֹ שָׁבַת֙ מִכׇּל־מְלַאכְתּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁר־בָּרָ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃{פ}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Elohim blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, for on it He abstained from all His work, which Elohim had created to do.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because in it He rested from all his work which God had created and performed.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And G-d blessed the seventh day [through the manna (a presage of the future), double the normal amount being provided on the sixth day], and He sanctified it, [through the manna, none falling on the Sabbath], for on it He rested from all of His work which the L-rd had created to do. [i.e., What was to have been done on the Sabbath was done on the sixth day, the work of that day being doubled.]


###### Genesis 2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/2:4)


אֵ֣לֶּה תוֹלְד֧וֹת הַשָּׁמַ֛יִם וְהָאָ֖רֶץ בְּהִבָּֽרְאָ֑ם בְּי֗וֹם עֲשׂ֛וֹת יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶ֥רֶץ וְשָׁמָֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
This is the history of the heavens and the earth when they were created, on the day when Adonoy Elohim made earth and heaven.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
These are the generations of the heaven and of the earth when they were created, in the day that the Lord God made the earth and the heavens.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
These [the above-mentioned] are the engenderings of the heaven and the earth, when they were created, on the day the L-rd G-d made earth and heaven [(whence it is derived that they were all created on the first day (see 1:14)].


###### Genesis 2:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/2:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/2:5)


וְכֹ֣ל**׀** שִׂ֣יחַ הַשָּׂדֶ֗ה טֶ֚רֶם יִֽהְיֶ֣ה בָאָ֔רֶץ וְכׇל־עֵ֥שֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה טֶ֣רֶם יִצְמָ֑ח כִּי֩ לֹ֨א הִמְטִ֜יר יְהֹוָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְאָדָ֣ם אַ֔יִן לַֽעֲבֹ֖ד אֶת־הָֽאֲדָמָֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
All the plants of the field were not yet on the earth, and all the herbal vegetation of the field had not yet sprouted, for Adonoy Elohim had not brought rain upon the earth, and there was [yet] no man to work the soil.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And no plant of the field was yet in the earth, and no herb of the field had yet grown: for the Lord God had not caused it to rain upon the earth, and there was not a man to till the ground.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And every plant of the field was not yet in the earth, and every grass of the field had not yet sprouted [above the ground (the third-day sprouting (12) remaining beneath the surface)], for the L-rd G-d [(the first, Yod-Key-Vav-Key, being His name; the second, Elokim, connoting Ruler and Judge)] had not yet caused it to rain upon the earth, for there was no man to work the ground [and to appreciate the rain, until Adam was created, who recognized that rain was needed for the world, prayed for it, and "secured" it].


###### Genesis 2:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/2:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/2:6)


וְאֵ֖ד יַֽעֲלֶ֣ה מִן־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְהִשְׁקָ֖ה אֶֽת־כׇּל־פְּנֵ֥י הָֽאֲדָמָֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
A mist rose up from the earth, and it watered the entire surface of the soil.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
But there went up a mist from the earth, and watered the whole face of the ground.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And [for the creation of man (1:27)] a vapor rose from the earth and watered the entire face of the ground, [water, as it were, being added to the "dough" for the "kneading" of man].


###### Genesis 2:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/2:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/2:7)


וַיִּ֩יצֶר֩ יְהֹוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶת־הָֽאָדָ֗ם עָפָר֙ מִן־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה וַיִּפַּ֥ח בְּאַפָּ֖יו נִשְׁמַ֣ת חַיִּ֑ים וַיְהִ֥י הָֽאָדָ֖ם לְנֶ֥פֶשׁ חַיָּֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Adonoy Elohim then formed the man, dust from the ground, and He blew into his nostrils the breath of life. And so man became a living soul.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the L-rd G-d formed (vayitzer) [two yods for two "formings," one for this world, one for the resurrection (as opposed to the creation of the beasts (19), where only one yod is written)] the man, dust from the [four corners of the] earth. And He blew into his nostrils a soul of life, and man became a vital soul, [having speech and understanding (as opposed to the beasts)].


###### Genesis 2:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/2:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/2:8)


וַיִּטַּ֞ע יְהֹוָ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים גַּן־בְּעֵ֖דֶן מִקֶּ֑דֶם וַיָּ֣שֶׂם שָׁ֔ם אֶת־הָֽאָדָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָצָֽר׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Adonoy Elohim planted a garden in Eden, to the east, and there He placed the man He had formed.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the Lord God planted a garden eastward in ῾Eden; and there He put the man whom He had formed.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the L-rd G-d planted a garden in Eden from the east, and He placed there the man that He had formed.


###### Genesis 2:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/2:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/2:9)


וַיַּצְמַ֞ח יְהֹוָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ מִן־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה כׇּל־עֵ֛ץ נֶחְמָ֥ד לְמַרְאֶ֖ה וְט֣וֹב לְמַאֲכָ֑ל וְעֵ֤ץ הַֽחַיִּים֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַגָּ֔ן וְעֵ֕ץ הַדַּ֖עַת ט֥וֹב וָרָֽע׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

###### Genesis 16:1

Avram’s wife Sarai had not borne him children. She had an Egyptian handmaid whose name was Hagar.

Now Saray Avram’s wife bore him no children: and she had a Miżrian handmaid, whose name was Hagar.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

###### Genesis 16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/16:2)

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Sarai said to Avram: Behold, the L-rd has held me back from bearing. Come, I pray you, to my handmaid. Perhaps I will be built up through her [in the merit of bringing my rival into my house]. And Avram heeded the voice [the Holy spirit] of Sarai.

## Chapter 42

###### Genesis 42:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/42:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/42:1)

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Jacob saw that there was a grain sale in Egypt. And Jacob said to his sons: Why should you be looked upon [strangely by others for not stocking up before your food gives out]?


###### Genesis 42:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/42:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/42:2)


וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּ֣ה שָׁמַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֥י יֶשׁ־שֶׁ֖בֶר בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם רְדוּ־שָׁ֙מָּה֙ וְשִׁבְרוּ־לָ֣נוּ מִשָּׁ֔ם וְנִחְיֶ֖ה וְלֹ֥א נָמֽוּת׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And he said, Behold, I have heard that there is corn in Miżrayim: go down there, and buy for us from there, that we may live, and not die.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And he said: Behold, I have heard that there is a (grain) sale in Egypt. Go down (redu) there [(the gematria of "redu" is 210, intimating the years of servitude in Egypt)], and buy grain for us from there so that we live and not die.


###### Genesis 42:3

וַיֵּרְד֥וּ אֲחֵֽי־יוֹסֵ֖ף עֲשָׂרָ֑ה לִשְׁבֹּ֥ר בָּ֖ר מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

###### Genesis 42:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/42:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Genesis/r/42:4)

# Exodus

שמות

Link: [https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus)

שעבוד בני ישראל במצרים, יציאת מצרים, מתן תורה ובניית המשכן.

The Israelites’ enslavement in Egypt, miraculous redemption, the giving of the Torah, and building of the Mishkan (Tabernacle).

Sections: Chapter-Verse

Location: Tanakh/Torah

Originally from [Sefaria](https://www.sefaria.org) via [TorahLM.org](https://torahlm.org) — see [licensing](https://torahlm.org/sefaria_license).

Version (He): Miqra according to the Masorah (Segments: 1210, License: CC-BY-SA)

Versions (En):

  - The Koren Jerusalem Bible (Segments: 1210, License: CC-BY-NC)
  - The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein (Segments: 1210, License: CC-BY)

**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Go, and gather the elders of Yisra᾽el together, and say to them, The Lord God of your fathers, the God of Avraham, of Yiżĥaq, and of Ya῾aqov, has appeared to me, saying, I have surely visited you, and seen that which is done to you in Miżrayim:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Go and gather the elders [i.e., the dignitaries] of Israel, and say to them: The L-rd, the G-d of your fathers, has appeared to me — the G-d of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — saying: I have remembered you ("pakod, etc.") and what has been done to you in Egypt.

###### Exodus 4:7

And he took it from his bosom, and, behold, it had resumed its fleshy appearance, [whence it is derived that G-d's goodly measure is more expeditious than His punitive one ("from his bosom," as opposed to "took it out," above, implying that it had healed upon contact with his bosom)].

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
“If they do not believe you, and they do not listen to the voice [of proof] of the first [miraculous] sign; then they will believe the voice [of proof] of the latter [second] sign.

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

###### Exodus 4:11

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

## Chapter 5

###### Exodus 5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:1)


וְאַחַ֗ר בָּ֚אוּ מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאַהֲרֹ֔ן וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֑ה כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהֹוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שַׁלַּח֙ אֶת־עַמִּ֔י וְיָחֹ֥גּוּ לִ֖י בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Afterwards Moshe and Aharon went and said to Pharaoh, “This is what Adonoy, God of Yisrael said, ‘Send My people, so they may celebrate a festival to Me in the wilderness.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And afterwards Moshe and Aharon went in, and told Par῾o, Thus says the Lord God of Yisra᾽el, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast to me in the wilderness.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And afterwards Moses and Aaron came [(but the elders, in fear of going, fell off one by one)], and they said to Pharaoh: Thus said the L-rd, the G-d of Israel: Send My people that they may make a festival unto Me in the desert.


###### Exodus 5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:2)


וַיֹּ֣אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֔ה מִ֤י יְהֹוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶשְׁמַ֣ע בְּקֹל֔וֹ לְשַׁלַּ֖ח אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לֹ֤א יָדַ֙עְתִּי֙ אֶת־יְהֹוָ֔ה וְגַ֥ם אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹ֥א אֲשַׁלֵּֽחַ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Pharaoh said, “Who is Adonoy that I should obey his voice, to let Yisrael go. I do not know Adonoy, nor will I let [the B’nei] Yisrael go.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And Par῾o said, Who is the Lord, that I should obey his voice to let Yisra᾽el go? I know not the Lord, nor will I let Yisra᾽el go.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Pharaoh said: Who is the L-rd that I should hearken to His voice to send out Israel? I do not know the L-rd and I shall also not send out Israel.


###### Exodus 5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:3)


וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֱלֹהֵ֥י הָעִבְרִ֖ים נִקְרָ֣א עָלֵ֑ינוּ נֵ֣לְכָה נָּ֡א דֶּ֩רֶךְ֩ שְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת יָמִ֜ים בַּמִּדְבָּ֗ר וְנִזְבְּחָה֙ לַֽיהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ פֶּ֨ן־יִפְגָּעֵ֔נוּ בַּדֶּ֖בֶר א֥וֹ בֶחָֽרֶב׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
They said [to him], “The God of the Hebrews has revealed Himself to us. Please allow us to take a three day journey into the wilderness, and let us sacrifice to Adonoy, our God, lest He strike us with the plague or with the sword.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And they said, The God of the Hebrews has met with us: let us go, we pray thee, three days’ journey into the desert, and sacrifice to the Lord our God; lest he fall upon us with pestilence, or with the sword.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And they said: The G-d of the Hebrews revealed Himself to us. Let us go, we pray you, a three days' distance in the desert and sacrifice to the L-rd our G-d lest He smite us [(instead of "smite you," in deference to royalty)] with pestilence or with the sword.


###### Exodus 5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:4)


וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם לָ֚מָּה מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאַהֲרֹ֔ן תַּפְרִ֥יעוּ אֶת־הָעָ֖ם מִֽמַּעֲשָׂ֑יו לְכ֖וּ לְסִבְלֹתֵיכֶֽם׃

The king of Egypt said to them, “Why, Moshe and Aharon, are you distracting the people from their work? Get back to your burdens.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the king of Miżrayim said to them, Why do you, Moshe and Aharon, distract the people from their works? get you to your burdens.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the king of Egypt said to them: Why, Moses and Aaron, would you distance the people from their work? Go to your labors [at home (the tribe of Levi being exempt from the servitude of Egypt)].


###### Exodus 5:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:5)


וַיֹּ֣אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֔ה הֵן־רַבִּ֥ים עַתָּ֖ה עַ֣ם הָאָ֑רֶץ וְהִשְׁבַּתֶּ֥ם אֹתָ֖ם מִסִּבְלֹתָֽם׃

וַיְצַ֥ו פַּרְעֹ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא אֶת־הַנֹּגְשִׂ֣ים בָּעָ֔ם וְאֶת־שֹׁטְרָ֖יו לֵאמֹֽר׃

###### Exodus 5:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:7)


לֹ֣א תֹאסִפ֞וּן לָתֵ֨ת תֶּ֧בֶן לָעָ֛ם לִלְבֹּ֥ן הַלְּבֵנִ֖ים כִּתְמ֣וֹל שִׁלְשֹׁ֑ם הֵ֚ם יֵֽלְכ֔וּ וְקֹשְׁשׁ֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם תֶּֽבֶן׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
“You shall no longer give the people straw to make bricks as before. Let them go gather [their own] straw,


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Do not continue to give stubble to the people [to knead with clay] to make bricks as heretofore. Let them go and collect stubble for themselves.


###### Exodus 5:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:8)


וְאֶת־מַתְכֹּ֨נֶת הַלְּבֵנִ֜ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֵם֩ עֹשִׂ֨ים תְּמ֤וֹל שִׁלְשֹׁם֙ תָּשִׂ֣ימוּ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם לֹ֥א תִגְרְע֖וּ מִמֶּ֑נּוּ כִּֽי־נִרְפִּ֣ים הֵ֔ם עַל־כֵּ֗ן הֵ֤ם צֹֽעֲקִים֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר נֵלְכָ֖ה נִזְבְּחָ֥ה לֵאלֹהֵֽינוּ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
[And] the quota of bricks that they made before, you shall place upon them; do not reduce it, for they are lazy and therefore they cry out, saying, ‘We want to go sacrifice to our God.’


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the quantity of the bricks, which they did make heretofore, you shall lay upon them; you shall not diminish aught of it: for they are idle; therefore they cry, saying, Let us go and sacrifice to our God.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the quota of bricks which they made heretofore you shall impose upon them. Do not reduce it. For they are idling. That is why are they crying out: "Let us go and sacrifice to our G-d!"


###### Exodus 5:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:9)


תִּכְבַּ֧ד הָעֲבֹדָ֛ה עַל־הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים וְיַעֲשׂוּ־בָ֑הּ וְאַל־יִשְׁע֖וּ בְּדִבְרֵי־שָֽׁקֶר׃

Make the workload heavier on the men, and make them do it. Let them not talk about false ideas.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Let more work be laid upon the men, that they may labour in it; and let them not regard vain words.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Let the labor be heavy on the men and let them do it, and let them not speak vain words.

וַיֵּ֨צְא֜וּ נֹגְשֵׂ֤י הָעָם֙ וְשֹׁ֣טְרָ֔יו וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ אֶל־הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר פַּרְעֹ֔ה אֵינֶ֛נִּי נֹתֵ֥ן לָכֶ֖ם תֶּֽבֶן׃

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

###### Exodus 5:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:11)


אַתֶּ֗ם לְכ֨וּ קְח֤וּ לָכֶם֙ תֶּ֔בֶן מֵאֲשֶׁ֖ר תִּמְצָ֑אוּ כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין נִגְרָ֛ע מֵעֲבֹדַתְכֶ֖ם דָּבָֽר׃

וַיָּ֥פֶץ הָעָ֖ם בְּכׇל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם לְקֹשֵׁ֥שׁ קַ֖שׁ לַתֶּֽבֶן׃

###### Exodus 5:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:13)


וְהַנֹּגְשִׂ֖ים אָצִ֣ים לֵאמֹ֑ר כַּלּ֤וּ מַעֲשֵׂיכֶם֙ דְּבַר־י֣וֹם בְּיוֹמ֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר בִּהְי֥וֹת הַתֶּֽבֶן׃

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

###### Exodus 5:14

וַיֻּכּ֗וּ שֹֽׁטְרֵי֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֣מוּ עֲלֵהֶ֔ם נֹגְשֵׂ֥י פַרְעֹ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר מַדּ֡וּעַ לֹא֩ כִלִּיתֶ֨ם חׇקְכֶ֤ם לִלְבֹּן֙ כִּתְמ֣וֹל שִׁלְשֹׁ֔ם גַּם־תְּמ֖וֹל גַּם־הַיּֽוֹם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The officers of the B’nei Yisrael were beaten—those whom Pharaoh’s taskmasters had appointed—and were told, “Why have you not completed your quotas of brick making as you did yesterday and before neither yesterday, nor today?”

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ שֹֽׁטְרֵי֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּצְעֲק֥וּ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר לָ֧מָּה תַעֲשֶׂ֦ה כֹ֖ה לַעֲבָדֶֽיךָ׃

תֶּ֗בֶן אֵ֤ין נִתָּן֙ לַעֲבָדֶ֔יךָ וּלְבֵנִ֛ים אֹמְרִ֥ים לָ֖נוּ עֲשׂ֑וּ וְהִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדֶ֛יךָ מֻכִּ֖ים וְחָטָ֥את עַמֶּֽךָ׃

###### Exodus 5:17

וַיֹּ֛אמֶר נִרְפִּ֥ים אַתֶּ֖ם נִרְפִּ֑ים עַל־כֵּן֙ אַתֶּ֣ם אֹֽמְרִ֔ים נֵלְכָ֖ה נִזְבְּחָ֥ה לַֽיהֹוָֽה׃

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

###### Exodus 5:18

וְעַתָּה֙ לְכ֣וּ עִבְד֔וּ וְתֶ֖בֶן לֹא־יִנָּתֵ֣ן לָכֶ֑ם וְתֹ֥כֶן לְבֵנִ֖ים תִּתֵּֽנוּ׃

###### Exodus 5:19

וַיִּרְא֞וּ שֹֽׁטְרֵ֧י בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֹתָ֖ם בְּרָ֣ע לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹא־תִגְרְע֥וּ מִלִּבְנֵיכֶ֖ם דְּבַר־י֥וֹם בְּיוֹמֽוֹ׃

The officers of the B’nei Yisrael realized their bad position, saying, “You must not reduce your daily quota of bricks.”

###### Exodus 5:20

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:20](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:20)


וַֽיִּפְגְּעוּ֙ אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאֶֽת־אַהֲרֹ֔ן נִצָּבִ֖ים לִקְרָאתָ֑ם בְּצֵאתָ֖ם מֵאֵ֥ת פַּרְעֹֽה׃

They met Moshe and Aharon who were waiting to meet them as they were leaving Pharaoh.

###### Exodus 5:21

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:21](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/5:21)


וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם יֵ֧רֶא יְהֹוָ֛ה עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם וְיִשְׁפֹּ֑ט אֲשֶׁ֧ר הִבְאַשְׁתֶּ֣ם אֶת־רֵיחֵ֗נוּ בְּעֵינֵ֤י פַרְעֹה֙ וּבְעֵינֵ֣י עֲבָדָ֔יו לָֽתֶת־חֶ֥רֶב בְּיָדָ֖ם לְהׇרְגֵֽנוּ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

And if you are a refuser, (not) to send out, behold, I shall smite all of your border with frogs.

This is not right. [Only] the [adult] men should go and worship Adonoy for this is what you desire.” He had them expelled from Pharaoh’s presence.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Not so: go now you that are men, and serve the Lord; for that is what you desire. And they were driven out from Par῾o’s presence.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Not so, [as you say, to take the children with you, but], let the men now go and serve the L-rd, for that [to sacrifice to the L-rd (3:18, 5:3)] is what you ask. And he [(It is not indicated who)] drove them away from Pharaoh's presence.

###### Exodus 11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/11:1)


וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה ע֣וֹד נֶ֤גַע אֶחָד֙ אָבִ֤יא עַל־פַּרְעֹה֙ וְעַל־מִצְרַ֔יִם אַֽחֲרֵי־כֵ֕ן יְשַׁלַּ֥ח אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִזֶּ֑ה כְּשַׁ֨לְּח֔וֹ כָּלָ֕ה גָּרֵ֛שׁ יְגָרֵ֥שׁ אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִזֶּֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Adonoy said to Moshe, “There is one more plague that I will bring upon Pharaoh and upon Egypt. After that he will send you away from here. When he sends you away, he will actually drive you out from here completely.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the Lord said to Moshe, Yet will I bring one plague more upon Par῾o, and upon Miżrayim; afterwards he will let you go from here: when he shall let you go, he shall surely thrust you out altogether from here.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the L-rd said to Moses: Yet one more plague shall I bring upon Pharaoh and upon Egypt. After that, he shall send you hence. When he sends (you), [he shall send] all [of you]; he shall drive you hence.


###### Exodus 11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/11:2)


דַּבֶּר־נָ֖א בְּאׇזְנֵ֣י הָעָ֑ם וְיִשְׁאֲל֞וּ אִ֣ישׁ**׀** מֵאֵ֣ת רֵעֵ֗הוּ וְאִשָּׁה֙ מֵאֵ֣ת רְעוּתָ֔הּ כְּלֵי־כֶ֖סֶף וּכְלֵ֥י זָהָֽב׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Speak, please, in the ears of the people, and let each man request [borrow] from his friend, and each woman from her friend, articles of silver and articles of gold.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Speak now in the ears of the people, and let every man ask of his neighbour, and every woman of her neighbour, jewels of silver, and jewels of gold.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Speak, I pray you, in the ears of the people, that every man ask of his (Egyptian) neighbor and every woman ask of her neighbor vessels of silver and vessels of gold, [so that the righteous one, Abraham, not say "and they shall serve them and they shall afflict them" (Genesis 15:3) He did fulfill, but "and afterwards they shall go out with great wealth" (Ibid. 14) He did not fulfill.]


###### Exodus 11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/11:3)


וַיִּתֵּ֧ן יְהֹוָ֛ה אֶת־חֵ֥ן הָעָ֖ם בְּעֵינֵ֣י מִצְרָ֑יִם גַּ֣ם**׀** הָאִ֣ישׁ מֹשֶׁ֗ה גָּד֤וֹל מְאֹד֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּעֵינֵ֥י עַבְדֵֽי־פַרְעֹ֖ה וּבְעֵינֵ֥י הָעָֽם׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Adonoy gave the people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians. Moshe too was very great in the land of Egypt, [both] in the eyes of Pharaoh’s servants and in the eyes of the people.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the Lord gave the people favour in the sight of Miżrayim; moreover the man Moshe was very great in the land of Miżrayim, in the sight of Par῾o’s servants, and in the sight of the people.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the L-rd put the favor of the people in the eyes of Egypt. The man Moses, too, was very great in the land of Egypt in the eyes of the servants of Pharaoh and in the eyes of the people.


###### Exodus 11:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/11:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/11:4)


וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֔ה כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהֹוָ֑ה כַּחֲצֹ֣ת הַלַּ֔יְלָה אֲנִ֥י יוֹצֵ֖א בְּת֥וֹךְ מִצְרָֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Moshe said, “This is what Adonoy has said, About the time of midnight, I will go out in the midst of Egypt.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And Moshe said, Thus says the Lord, About midnight will I go out into the midst of Miżrayim:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Moses said [to Pharaoh]: Thus said the L-rd: When the night is divided [i.e., at midnight] I shall go out into the midst of Egypt.


###### Exodus 11:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/11:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/11:5)


וּמֵ֣ת כׇּל־בְּכוֹר֮ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֒יִם֒ מִבְּכ֤וֹר פַּרְעֹה֙ הַיֹּשֵׁ֣ב עַל־כִּסְא֔וֹ עַ֚ד בְּכ֣וֹר הַשִּׁפְחָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר אַחַ֣ר הָרֵחָ֑יִם וְכֹ֖ל בְּכ֥וֹר בְּהֵמָֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Every first-born in the land of Egypt will die, from the first-born of Pharaoh sitting on his throne, to the first-born of the [Egyptian] slave girl, behind the mill-stones, and every first-born animal.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and all the firstborn in the land of Miżrayim shall die, from the firstborn of Par῾o that sits on his throne, even to the firstborn of the maidservant that is behind the mill; and all the firstborn of cattle.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And every first-born in the land of Egypt will die, from the first-born of Pharaoh who sits on his throne [(and down)] until the first-born of the maidservant behind the mill-stones [(and up. The captive first-born (see 12:29) died so that they not say that their gods "claimed their shame" and brought destruction upon the Egyptians. The sons of the maidservants died, for they, too, worked the Jews and rejoiced in their affliction)] and all the first-born of beasts, [these having been served as objects of idolatry. ("When the Holy One Blessed be He exacts punishment of a nation, He exacts punishment of its gods.")]


###### Exodus 11:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/11:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/11:6)


וְהָ֥יְתָ֛ה צְעָקָ֥ה גְדֹלָ֖ה בְּכׇל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם אֲשֶׁ֤ר כָּמֹ֙הוּ֙ לֹ֣א נִהְיָ֔תָה וְכָמֹ֖הוּ לֹ֥א תֹסִֽף׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
There will be a great cry [of anguish] throughout the entire land of Egypt, the likes of which there never was and like there never will be.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And there shall be a great cry throughout all the land of Miżrayim, such as there was none like it, nor shall be like it any more.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And there will be a great outcry in the whole land of Egypt, the like of which had never been and the like of which will not be again.


###### Exodus 11:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/11:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/11:7)


וּלְכֹ֣ל**׀** בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לֹ֤א יֶֽחֱרַץ־כֶּ֙לֶב֙ לְשֹׁנ֔וֹ לְמֵאִ֖ישׁ וְעַד־בְּהֵמָ֑ה לְמַ֙עַן֙ תֵּֽדְע֔וּן אֲשֶׁר֙ יַפְלֶ֣ה יְהֹוָ֔ה בֵּ֥ין מִצְרַ֖יִם וּבֵ֥ין יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
But among all the B’nei Yisrael, a dog will not sharpen its tongue [growl] at man or animal. You will then know that Adonoy distinguishes between Egypt and Yisrael.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
But against any of the children of Yisra᾽el not a dog shall move its tongue, neither against man or beast: that you may know that the Lord differentiates between Miżrayim and between Yisra᾽el.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And against all the children of Israel a dog shall not sharpen its tongue — from man until beast — so that you will know that the L-rd distinguished between Egypt and Israel.


###### Exodus 11:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/11:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/11:8)


וְיָרְד֣וּ כׇל־עֲבָדֶ֩יךָ֩ אֵ֨לֶּה אֵלַ֜י וְהִשְׁתַּֽחֲווּ־לִ֣י לֵאמֹ֗ר צֵ֤א אַתָּה֙ וְכׇל־הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־בְּרַגְלֶ֔יךָ וְאַחֲרֵי־כֵ֖ן אֵצֵ֑א וַיֵּצֵ֥א מֵֽעִם־פַּרְעֹ֖ה בׇּחֳרִי־אָֽף׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Then all these, your servants, will come down to me, and prostrate themselves saying, ‘Go! You and all the people that follow you. Then I will go out.” He [Moshe] then left Pharaoh in great anger.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And all these thy servants shall come down to me, and bow down themselves to me, saying, Get thee gone, and all the people that follow thee: and after that I will go out. And he went out from Par῾o in great anger.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And all these servants of yours will come down and bow down to me, saying: Go out! you and all your followers; and then I will go out. And [after he finished what he had to say] he went out from before Pharaoh in great wrath [over his having said (10:28): "You shall not see my face again!"]


###### Exodus 11:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/11:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/11:9)


וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה לֹא־יִשְׁמַ֥ע אֲלֵיכֶ֖ם פַּרְעֹ֑ה לְמַ֛עַן רְב֥וֹת מוֹפְתַ֖י בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Adonoy said to Moshe, “Pharaoh will not listen to you. Thus I will multiply My wonders in the land of Egypt.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the Lord said to Moshe, Par῾o shall not hearken to you; that my wonders may be multiplied in the land of Miżrayim.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the L-rd said to Moses: Pharaoh will not pay heed to you, so that My wonders be multiplied in the land of Egypt [viz.: the plague of the first-born, the splitting of the Red Sea, and the "shaking out" of the Egyptians therein.]


###### Exodus 11:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/11:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/11:10)


וּמֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאַהֲרֹ֗ן עָשׂ֛וּ אֶת־כׇּל־הַמֹּפְתִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה לִפְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה וַיְחַזֵּ֤ק יְהֹוָה֙ אֶת־לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְלֹֽא־שִׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵאַרְצֽוֹ׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Moshe and Aharon had done all these wonders before Pharaoh. [However] Adonoy hardened Pharaoh’s heart and he did not send the B’nei Yisrael out of his land.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And Moshe and Aharon did all these wonders before Par῾o: and the Lord hardened Par῾o’s heart, so that he would not let the children of Yisra᾽el go out of his land.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Moses and Aaron performed all of these wonders before Pharaoh, and the L-rd strengthened Pharaoh's heart and he did not send the children of Israel from his land.



## Chapter 12

###### Exodus 12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:1)


וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֔ן בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם לֵאמֹֽר׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Adonoy said to Moshe and Aharon in the land of Egypt saying:


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the Lord spoke to Moshe and Aharon in the land of Miżrayim, saying,


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the L-rd said to Moses and to Aaron [(Aaron being accorded honor in this first mitzvah (2) for having participated and exerted himself along with Moses in the embassy of the signs)] in the land of Egypt [outside the city (see 11:29)], saying:


###### Exodus 12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:2)


הַחֹ֧דֶשׁ הַזֶּ֛ה לָכֶ֖ם רֹ֣אשׁ חֳדָשִׁ֑ים רִאשׁ֥וֹן הוּא֙ לָכֶ֔ם לְחׇדְשֵׁ֖י הַשָּׁנָֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
“This month shall be [reckoned] to you [as] the head [beginning] of months. It shall be to you the first of the months of the year.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
This month shall be to you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
This month [this stage of the moon (the L-rd "pointing it out" to Moses)] [Nissan] shall be to you the beginning of months. It is the first for you of the months of the year.


###### Exodus 12:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:3)


דַּבְּר֗וּ אֶֽל־כׇּל־עֲדַ֤ת יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בֶּעָשֹׂ֖ר לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַזֶּ֑ה וְיִקְח֣וּ לָהֶ֗ם אִ֛ישׁ שֶׂ֥ה לְבֵית־אָבֹ֖ת שֶׂ֥ה לַבָּֽיִת׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Speak to the entire community of Israel saying, ‘On the tenth [day] of this month they shall take—each man [shall take] a lamb for [his] family, a lamb for each household.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Speak to all the congregation of Yisra᾽el, saying, On the tenth day of this month they shall take to them every man a lamb, according to the house of their fathers, a lamb for a house:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Speak [today, on Rosh Chodesh] to the whole congregation of Israel, saying: On the tenth day of this month [(the "taking" of the paschal lamb of Egypt was on the tenth, but not that of future generations)] shall they take for themselves, each man a lamb for a family [(and, in the event that the family is large and one lamb will not suffice for it)], a lamb for a household [(i.e., for each household within that family)].


###### Exodus 12:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:4)


וְאִם־יִמְעַ֣ט הַבַּ֘יִת֮ מִהְי֣וֹת מִשֶּׂה֒ וְלָקַ֣ח ה֗וּא וּשְׁכֵנ֛וֹ הַקָּרֹ֥ב אֶל־בֵּית֖וֹ בְּמִכְסַ֣ת נְפָשֹׁ֑ת אִ֚ישׁ לְפִ֣י אׇכְל֔וֹ תָּכֹ֖סּוּ עַל־הַשֶּֽׂה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If the [members of the] household are too few for the [eating of a] lamb then he shall take [a lamb] [together] with his neighbor, close by his house, according to the number of individuals. According to what the person eats shall you make your count regarding the lamb.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and if the household be too little for a lamb, let him and his neighbour next to his house take it according to the number of the souls; according to every man’s eating shall you make your count for the lamb.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if the household is too small for one lamb [so that some of it would be left over (nothar, which is forbidden)], then he and his neighbor next to his house shall take it according to the count of souls. Each according to his eating [(excluding one who is so sick or old that he cannot eat at least an olive size)] shall you [include in the] count for the lamb.


###### Exodus 12:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:5)


שֶׂ֥ה תָמִ֛ים זָכָ֥ר בֶּן־שָׁנָ֖ה יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם מִן־הַכְּבָשִׂ֥ים וּמִן־הָעִזִּ֖ים תִּקָּֽחוּ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
A flawless lamb, a yearling male must be in your possession. You may take it from sheep or goats.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male of the first year: you shall take it from the sheep, or from the goats:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
A lamb, unblemished, a one-year-old male [i.e., in its first year] shall it be to you. Of the lambs or of the goats shall you take it, [a (young) goat, too, being regarded as a "lamb"].


###### Exodus 12:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:6)


וְהָיָ֤ה לָכֶם֙ לְמִשְׁמֶ֔רֶת עַ֣ד אַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָׂ֛ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַזֶּ֑ה וְשָׁחֲט֣וּ אֹת֗וֹ כֹּ֛ל קְהַ֥ל עֲדַֽת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בֵּ֥ין הָעַרְבָּֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You shall hold it in safekeeping until the fourteenth day of this month, they shall slaughter it—the entire community of Yisrael—between evenings [in the afternoon].


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and you shall keep it until the fourteenth day of the same month: and the whole assembly of the congregation of Yisra᾽el shall kill it towards evening.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And it shall be to you for a keeping [i.e., surveillance against blemish] until the fourteenth day of this month [(Israel being given two mitzvoth on that night — the blood of the paschal lamb and the blood of circumcision — to make them worthy of redemption)], and the entire congregation of Israel shall slaughter it [(whence it is derived that one's messenger is reckoned as the sender himself)], from midday (on).


###### Exodus 12:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:7)


וְלָֽקְחוּ֙ מִן־הַדָּ֔ם וְנָ֥תְנ֛וּ עַל־שְׁתֵּ֥י הַמְּזוּזֹ֖ת וְעַל־הַמַּשְׁק֑וֹף עַ֚ל הַבָּ֣תִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־יֹאכְל֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ בָּהֶֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
They shall take of its blood and place it on the side of the doorposts and on the lintel of the houses in which they will eat [the lamb].


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And they shall take the blood, and put it on the two side posts and on the upper door post of the houses, in which they shall eat it.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And they shall take from the blood [in the basin] and place it on the two side posts and on the lintel of the houses where they shall eat it, [but not on non-dwellings].


###### Exodus 12:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:8)


וְאָכְל֥וּ אֶת־הַבָּשָׂ֖ר בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַזֶּ֑ה צְלִי־אֵ֣שׁ וּמַצּ֔וֹת עַל־מְרֹרִ֖ים יֹאכְלֻֽהוּ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
They shall eat the meat during this night. It shall be roasted over fire. They shall eat it with matzos and bitter herbs.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And they shall eat the meat in that night, roast with fire, and unleavened bread; and with bitter herbs they shall eat it.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And they shall eat the flesh, [but not sinews and bones] on this night, roasted in fire. And matzoth with merorim [(Every bitter herb is called maror)] shall they eat it, [in commemoration of (1:10): "And they embittered (vayemararu) their lives."]


###### Exodus 12:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:9)


אַל־תֹּאכְל֤וּ מִמֶּ֙נּוּ֙ נָ֔א וּבָשֵׁ֥ל מְבֻשָּׁ֖ל בַּמָּ֑יִם כִּ֣י אִם־צְלִי־אֵ֔שׁ רֹאשׁ֥וֹ עַל־כְּרָעָ֖יו וְעַל־קִרְבּֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You must not eat it half-cooked or boiled in water, but only roasted over fire, its head with its knees and its inner organs.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Eat not of it raw, nor boiled at all in water, but roast with fire; its head with its legs, and with its entrails.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Do not eat of it not entirely roasted or cooked in water [or any other liquid], but roasted in fire [(a negative commandment here being added to the positive (8)]; [it is to be roasted entire], its head, with its legs, with its inner parts, [and its entrails placed therein after rinsing].


###### Exodus 12:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:10)


וְלֹא־תוֹתִ֥ירוּ מִמֶּ֖נּוּ עַד־בֹּ֑קֶר וְהַנֹּתָ֥ר מִמֶּ֛נּוּ עַד־בֹּ֖קֶר בָּאֵ֥שׁ תִּשְׂרֹֽפוּ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You must not leave any of it over until morning. Any of it left over until morning must be burned in fire.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And you shall let nothing of it remain until the morning; and that which remains of it until the morning you shall burn with fire.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall not leave over anything of it until the morning [(sunrise)]; and what is left over of it until morning [(dawn)], in fire shall you burn it.


###### Exodus 12:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:11)


וְכָ֘כָה֮ תֹּאכְל֣וּ אֹתוֹ֒ מׇתְנֵיכֶ֣ם חֲגֻרִ֔ים נַֽעֲלֵיכֶם֙ בְּרַגְלֵיכֶ֔ם וּמַקֶּלְכֶ֖ם בְּיֶדְכֶ֑ם וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֤ם אֹתוֹ֙ בְּחִפָּז֔וֹן פֶּ֥סַח ה֖וּא לַיהֹוָֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
This is how you must eat it: with your waist belted, your shoes on your feet, and your staff in your hand. You must eat it in haste, it is a Pesach-offering to Adonoy.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thus shall you eat it; with your loins girded, your shoes on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and you shall eat it in haste; it is the Lord’s passover.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And thus shall you eat it: your thighs girded ["ready for the road"], your shoes on your feet, and your staff in your hand. And you shall eat it in haste — it is a pesach ("skipping over") offering to the L-rd [see 27].


###### Exodus 12:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:12)


וְעָבַרְתִּ֣י בְאֶֽרֶץ־מִצְרַ֘יִם֮ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַזֶּה֒ וְהִכֵּיתִ֤י כׇל־בְּכוֹר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם מֵאָדָ֖ם וְעַד־בְּהֵמָ֑ה וּבְכׇל־אֱלֹהֵ֥י מִצְרַ֛יִם אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֥ה שְׁפָטִ֖ים אֲנִ֥י יְהֹוָֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
I will pass through the land of Egypt on that night, and I will strike [kill] every first-born in the land of Egypt, from man to beast; and against all the gods of Egypt, I will execute judgments, I am Adonoy.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For I will pass through the land of Miżrayim this night, and will smite all the firstborn in the land of Miżrayim, both man and beast: and against all the gods of Miżrayim I will execute judgments: I am the Lord.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And I shall pass through the land of Egypt in this night, and I shall smite every first-born in the land of Egypt [(even first-born of other nations in the land of Egypt)], from man until beast; and upon all the gods of Egypt I shall wreak judgments, [wooden idols rotting and metal ones melting]; I am the L-rd [I shall do this Myself and not through a messenger.]


###### Exodus 12:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:13)


וְהָיָה֩ הַדָּ֨ם לָכֶ֜ם לְאֹ֗ת עַ֤ל הַבָּתִּים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתֶּ֣ם שָׁ֔ם וְרָאִ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־הַדָּ֔ם וּפָסַחְתִּ֖י עֲלֵכֶ֑ם וְלֹֽא־יִֽהְיֶ֨ה בָכֶ֥ם נֶ֙גֶף֙ לְמַשְׁחִ֔ית בְּהַכֹּתִ֖י בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The blood will be for you as a sign on the houses where you are [staying]. I will see the blood and I will pass over you. There will be no plague against you when I strike the land of Egypt.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where you are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Miżrayim.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the blood shall be for you as a sign [("for you" and not "for others" — whence it is inferred that the blood was placed on the inside)] upon the houses where you are, and I shall see the blood [i.e., I shall "give heart" to your performance of My mitzvoth], and I shall skip over you, and there will be no destroying plague in you when I smite the land of Egypt [(even if you are found in an Egyptian house — but there will be plague in an Egyptian found in an Israelite house)].


###### Exodus 12:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:14)


וְהָיָה֩ הַיּ֨וֹם הַזֶּ֤ה לָכֶם֙ לְזִכָּר֔וֹן וְחַגֹּתֶ֥ם אֹת֖וֹ חַ֣ג לַֽיהֹוָ֑ה לְדֹרֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם חֻקַּ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם תְּחׇגֻּֽהוּ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
This day shall be for you a [day of] remembrance. You shall celebrate it as a festival to Adonoy, throughout your generations. It is an eternal statute that you must celebrate it.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And this day shall be to you for a memorial; and you shall keep it a feast to the Lord; throughout your generations shall you keep it a feast by ordinance for ever.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And this day [of the exodus] shall be for you as a remembrance [for the coming generations], and you shall celebrate it [the fifteenth of Nissan] as a festival of the L-rd. For your generations as an everlasting statute shall you celebrate it.


###### Exodus 12:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:15)


שִׁבְעַ֤ת יָמִים֙ מַצּ֣וֹת תֹּאכֵ֔לוּ אַ֚ךְ בַּיּ֣וֹם הָרִאשׁ֔וֹן תַּשְׁבִּ֥יתוּ שְּׂאֹ֖ר מִבָּתֵּיכֶ֑ם כִּ֣י**׀** כׇּל־אֹכֵ֣ל חָמֵ֗ץ וְנִכְרְתָ֞ה הַנֶּ֤פֶשׁ הַהִוא֙ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִיּ֥וֹם הָרִאשֹׁ֖ן עַד־י֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִעִֽי׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You must eat matzos for seven days, but before the first day you must remove [all] leaven from your homes; for anyone who eats chametz, that soul will be cut off from Yisrael. [Chametz is forbidden] from the first day [of Pesach] until [after] the seventh day.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Seven days shall you eat unleavened bread; but on the first day you shall have put away leaven out of your houses: for whoever eats leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Yisra᾽el.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Seven days [lit., "a septet of days"] shall you eat matzoth. [(Eating matzoth on the first night is obligatory, and, thereafter, optional)] But on the first day [i.e., on the eve of Pesach] you shall eliminate leaven from your houses. For whoever eats chametz, that soul [(one who has volition, but not one who is forced)] shall be cut off from Israel [and from My presence] — from the first day until the seventh day.


###### Exodus 12:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:16)


וּבַיּ֤וֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן֙ מִקְרָא־קֹ֔דֶשׁ וּבַיּוֹם֙ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י מִקְרָא־קֹ֖דֶשׁ יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם כׇּל־מְלָאכָה֙ לֹא־יֵעָשֶׂ֣ה בָהֶ֔ם אַ֚ךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵאָכֵ֣ל לְכׇל־נֶ֔פֶשׁ ה֥וּא לְבַדּ֖וֹ יֵעָשֶׂ֥ה לָכֶֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The first day shall be a holy assembly and the seventh day shall be a holy assembly to you. No work shall be done on them, only for [the preparation of food] which will be eaten by every person, that alone may be done for you.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And on the first day there shall be a holy gathering, and on the seventh day there shall be a holy gathering to you; no manner of work shall be done on them, save that which every person must eat, that only may be done by you.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And on the first day a calling of holiness and on the seventh day a calling of holiness shall there be unto you. [Call it "holy" for purposes of eating, drinking, and raiment.] No labor shall be done in them [even through a non-Jew]. Only what is to be eaten by all souls, that [labor] alone may be done for you, [and not any preparatory labor which could have been done before the festival].


###### Exodus 12:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:17)


וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם֮ אֶת־הַמַּצּוֹת֒ כִּ֗י בְּעֶ֙צֶם֙ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה הוֹצֵ֥אתִי אֶת־צִבְאוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֞ם אֶת־הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֛ה לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶ֖ם חֻקַּ֥ת עוֹלָֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You must be vigilant regarding the matzos, for on this very day I brought out your hosts from the land of Egypt. You must preserve this day for your generations, it is an eternal statute.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And you shall observe the commandment of unleavened bread; for on this very day have I brought your hosts out of the land of Miżrayim: therefore shall you observe this day in your generations by an ordinance for ever.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall watch over the matzoth [that they not become chametz]; for on this very same day I took your hosts out from the land of Egypt. And you shall guard this day [against performing labor thereon] unto your generations as an everlasting statute.


###### Exodus 12:18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:18)


בָּרִאשֹׁ֡ן בְּאַרְבָּעָה֩ עָשָׂ֨ר י֤וֹם לַחֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ בָּעֶ֔רֶב תֹּאכְל֖וּ מַצֹּ֑ת עַ֠ד י֣וֹם הָאֶחָ֧ד וְעֶשְׂרִ֛ים לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ בָּעָֽרֶב׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
In the first [month] on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening you shall eat matzos; until the twenty-first day of the month in the evening.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at evening, shall you eat unleavened bread, until the twenty first day of the month at evening.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
On the first day, on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening shall you eat matzoth, until the twenty-first day of the month in the evening [(whence it is derived that the mitzvah obtains in the evenings, too)].


###### Exodus 12:19

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:19](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:19)


שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֔ים שְׂאֹ֕ר לֹ֥א יִמָּצֵ֖א בְּבָתֵּיכֶ֑ם כִּ֣י**׀** כׇּל־אֹכֵ֣ל מַחְמֶ֗צֶת וְנִכְרְתָ֞ה הַנֶּ֤פֶשׁ הַהִוא֙ מֵעֲדַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בַּגֵּ֖ר וּבְאֶזְרַ֥ח הָאָֽרֶץ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
For seven days leaven may not be found in your homes, for whoever eats chametz that soul shall be cut off from the community of Israel, whether a proselyte or a native born in the land.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Seven days shall there be no leaven found in your houses: for whoever eats that which is leavened, even that soul shall be cut off from the congregation of Yisra᾽el, whether he be a stranger, or born in the land.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Seven days, se'or [a leavening agent] shall not be found in your houses [i.e., under your control — to exclude liability for chametz of a non-Jew which is found in a Jew's property.] For whoever eats leavening, that soul shall be cut off from the congregation of Israel, whether he be a proselyte [(for whom the miracle was not performed)] or a citizen of the land.


###### Exodus 12:20

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:20](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:20)


כׇּל־מַחְמֶ֖צֶת לֹ֣א תֹאכֵ֑לוּ בְּכֹל֙ מוֹשְׁבֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם תֹּאכְל֖וּ מַצּֽוֹת׃{פ}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You must not eat anything that is chametz. In all your dwellings you shall eat matzos.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
You shall eat nothing leavened; in all your habitations shall you eat unleavened bread.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
All leavening [(including an admixture — this is the exhortation against the eating of se'or)] you shall not eat. In all of your habitations shall you eat matzoth [(to exclude — as satisfying the mitzvah— matzoth of ma'aser sheni and thanksgiving challoth, which may be eaten only in Jerusalem)].


###### Exodus 12:21

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:21](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:21)


וַיִּקְרָ֥א מֹשֶׁ֛ה לְכׇל־זִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֑ם מִֽשְׁכ֗וּ וּקְח֨וּ לָכֶ֥ם צֹ֛אן לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתֵיכֶ֖ם וְשַׁחֲט֥וּ הַפָּֽסַח׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Moshe called to all the elders of Yisrael, and he said to them, “Draw [from your flocks] or purchase for yourselves a lamb for your families and slaughter it as a Pesach offering.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Then Moshe called for all the elders of Yisra᾽el, and said to them, Draw out and take you lambs according to your families, and kill the passover.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Moses called to all the elders of Israel, and he said to them: Draw forth [if you have your own,] and take unto yourselves [i.e., buy, if you do not have your own,] sheep for your families [a lamb for a family], and slaughter the pesach.


###### Exodus 12:22

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:22](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:22)


וּלְקַחְתֶּ֞ם אֲגֻדַּ֣ת אֵז֗וֹב וּטְבַלְתֶּם֮ בַּדָּ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־בַּסַּף֒ וְהִגַּעְתֶּ֤ם אֶל־הַמַּשְׁקוֹף֙ וְאֶל־שְׁתֵּ֣י הַמְּזוּזֹ֔ת מִן־הַדָּ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּסָּ֑ף וְאַתֶּ֗ם לֹ֥א תֵצְא֛וּ אִ֥ישׁ מִפֶּֽתַח־בֵּית֖וֹ עַד־בֹּֽקֶר׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the blood that is in the basin. Touch the lintel and the two side [door] posts with some of the blood in the basin. And all of you, let no man go out the door of his house until morning.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the blood that is in the basin, and touch with it the lintel and the two side posts, with the blood that is in the basin; and none of you shall go out at the door of his house until the morning.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall take a bundle [three stalks] of hyssop and dip it in the blood which is in the basin, and touch the lintel and the two doorposts (with some) of the blood which is in the basin, [a new dipping for each touching]; and you, do not go out, a man from the door of his house until morning. ["Once 'the destroyer' has been granted leave to destroy, he does not distinguish between righteous and wicked."]


###### Exodus 12:23

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:23](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:23)


וְעָבַ֣ר יְהֹוָה֮ לִנְגֹּ֣ף אֶת־מִצְרַ֒יִם֒ וְרָאָ֤ה אֶת־הַדָּם֙ עַל־הַמַּשְׁק֔וֹף וְעַ֖ל שְׁתֵּ֣י הַמְּזוּזֹ֑ת וּפָסַ֤ח יְהֹוָה֙ עַל־הַפֶּ֔תַח וְלֹ֤א יִתֵּן֙ הַמַּשְׁחִ֔ית לָבֹ֥א אֶל־בָּתֵּיכֶ֖ם לִנְגֹּֽף׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Adonoy will pass through to plague the Egyptians and He will see the blood on the lintel and on the two side [door] posts. Adonoy will then pass over that door and will not allow the destroyer to enter your houses to plague you.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For the Lord will pass through to smite Miżrayim; and when he sees the blood upon the lintel, and on the two side posts, the Lord will pass over the door, and will not allow the destroyer to come into your houses to smite you.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the L-rd will pass through to smite Egypt, and He will see the blood on the lintel and on the two door posts, and the L-rd will skip over the door, and He will not permit the destroyer to come to your houses to smite.


###### Exodus 12:24

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:24](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:24)


וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה לְחׇק־לְךָ֥ וּלְבָנֶ֖יךָ עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You must preserve this [ritual] as a statute for you and your children forever.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And you shall observe this thing for an ordinance to thee and to thy sons for ever.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall keep this thing as a statute for you and for your children forever.


###### Exodus 12:25

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:25](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:25)


וְהָיָ֞ה כִּֽי־תָבֹ֣אוּ אֶל־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִתֵּ֧ן יְהֹוָ֛ה לָכֶ֖ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֵּ֑ר וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־הָעֲבֹדָ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
When you come to the land that Adonoy will give to you, as He spoke, you must preserve this service.

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And every man-servant acquired by money — you shall circumcise him; then shall he [(according to one view, the master; according to another, the servant)] eat of it.

An [alien] sojourner or hired worker may not eat it.

A foreigner and a hired servant shall not eat of it.

A sojourner [a ger toshav (one who does not convert fully, but who undertakes not to serve idols and to observe the seven Noahide laws)] and a hired man [a non-Jew] may not eat of it. [The above applies (even) to a circumcised Arab or a circumcised Giveonite who is a sojourner or a hired man.]

The entire community of Yisrael must make this [offering].

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
When a proselyte dwells with you and wants to make the Pesach-offering to Adonoy, every male must be circumcised. He may then come near [join] to make it, and be like the native born. But no uncircumcised male may eat of it.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

And he shall be as the citizen of the land, and no uncircumcised one shall eat of it [(including one who is not circumcised because his brothers have died as a result of circumcision)].

###### Exodus 13:12

###### Exodus 13:13

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And every firstling of an ass [and not of any other unclean beast, the first-born of the Egyptians being compared to asses, and, also, because the asses "assisted" Israel in taking out the spoils of Egypt)] shall you redeem with a lamb. [The lamb is given to the Cohein, benefit may then be derived from the firstling, and the lamb is chullin (non-sacred) for the Cohein.] And if you do not redeem it, then you shall break its neck [with a hatchet from behind (He caused the Cohein a loss; therefore, he suffers a loss)], and every human first-born among your sons shall you redeem [by giving five selaim to the Cohein].
