**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
[Then] Moshe said, “When Adonoy gives you meat to eat in the evening, and a filling meal of bread in the morning, Adonoy will have heard your complaints, that you cause complaints against Him. What are we? Your complaints are not against us but against Adonoy.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And Moshe said, This shall be, when the Lord shall give you in the evening meat to eat, and in the morning your fill of bread; when the Lord hears your murmurings which you murmur against him: and what are we? your murmurings are not against us, but against the Lord.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Moses said: (You will see this) when the L-rd gives to you in the evening flesh to eat, and bread in the morning to satiety [(but not flesh to satiety — whence we infer that flesh is not to be eaten to satiety)], for the L-rd hears your cavilings whereby you cause [others] to cavil against Him. And what are we? Not against us are your cavilings, but against the L-rd.

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

## Chapter 17

###### Exodus 17:1

וַ֠יִּסְע֠וּ כׇּל־עֲדַ֨ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל מִמִּדְבַּר־סִ֛ין לְמַסְעֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־פִּ֣י יְהֹוָ֑ה וַֽיַּחֲנוּ֙ בִּרְפִידִ֔ים וְאֵ֥ין מַ֖יִם לִשְׁתֹּ֥ת הָעָֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/17:2)

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

###### Exodus 17:5

וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה עֲבֹר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם וְקַ֥ח אִתְּךָ֖ מִזִּקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּמַטְּךָ֗ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִכִּ֤יתָ בּוֹ֙ אֶת־הַיְאֹ֔ר קַ֥ח בְּיָדְךָ֖ וְהָלָֽכְתָּ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

###### Exodus 17:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/17:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/17:6)


הִנְנִ֣י עֹמֵד֩ לְפָנֶ֨יךָ שָּׁ֥ם׀עַֽל־הַצּוּר֮ בְּחֹרֵב֒ וְהִכִּ֣יתָ בַצּ֗וּר וְיָצְא֥וּ מִמֶּ֛נּוּ מַ֖יִם וְשָׁתָ֣ה הָעָ֑ם וַיַּ֤עַשׂ כֵּן֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֖י זִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

###### Exodus 17:7

וַיִּקְרָא֙ שֵׁ֣ם הַמָּק֔וֹם מַסָּ֖ה וּמְרִיבָ֑ה עַל־רִ֣יב**׀** בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְעַ֨ל נַסֹּתָ֤ם אֶת־יְהֹוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הֲיֵ֧שׁ יְהֹוָ֛ה בְּקִרְבֵּ֖נוּ אִם־אָֽיִן׃{פ}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

###### Exodus 17:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/17:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/17:9)


וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֤ה אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֙עַ֙ בְּחַר־לָ֣נוּ אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְצֵ֖א הִלָּחֵ֣ם בַּעֲמָלֵ֑ק מָחָ֗ר אָנֹכִ֤י נִצָּב֙ עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ הַגִּבְעָ֔ה וּמַטֵּ֥ה הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּיָדִֽי׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

## Chapter 19

###### Exodus 19:1

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
On the third month of the exodus of the children of Israel from the land of Egypt, on this day [on the New Moon ("Let words of Torah always be 'new' to you, as if they were given this day")], they came to the desert of Sinai.


###### Exodus 19:2

###### Exodus 19:3

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

Even the kohanim who [usually] come near to Adonoy’s Presence, must be sanctified, lest Adonoy send destruction among them.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And let the priests also, who come near to the Lord, sanctify themselves, lest the Lord break forth upon them.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And also the priests [i.e., the first-born], who draw near to the L-rd [to offer sacrifices], let them [not ascend, but let them] be in readiness [to take their assigned stations], lest the L-rd [kill them and] make a breach in them.


###### Exodus 19:23

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/19:23](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/19:23)

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Moshe said to Adonoy, “The people can not go up to Mount Sinai, for You have warned us saying, ‘Set a boundary around the mountain and sanctify it.’”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And Moshe said to the Lord, The people cannot come up to mount Sinay: for thou didst charge us, saying, Set bounds about the mountain, and sanctify it.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Moses said to the L-rd: The people will not be able to ascend Mount Sinai, for You [already] warned us, saying: Demarcate bounds for the mountain and hallow it. [There is no need, then, for me to warn them again.]


###### Exodus 19:24

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/19:24](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/19:24)


וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֤יו יְהֹוָה֙ לֶךְ־רֵ֔ד וְעָלִ֥יתָ אַתָּ֖ה וְאַהֲרֹ֣ן עִמָּ֑ךְ וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים וְהָעָ֗ם אַל־יֶֽהֶרְס֛וּ לַעֲלֹ֥ת אֶל־יְהֹוָ֖ה פֶּן־יִפְרׇץ־בָּֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Adonoy said to him, “Go down. You will then come up [again], along with Aharon. The kohanim and the people, [however,] must not break through to go up toward [the Presence of] Adonoy, lest He send destruction among them.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the Lord said to him. Go, get thee down, and thou shalt come up, thou, and Aharon with thee: but let not the priests and the people break through to come up to the Lord, lest he break forth upon them.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the L-rd said to him: Go, descend, [and warn them again, (prompting to zeal being called for both before the deed and at the time of the deed)], and go up, you [in your precincts] and Aaron with you [in his precincts], and the priests [in their precincts] — and the people, let them not break [their bounds at all] to ascend to the L-rd, lest He make a breach in them.

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Moshe went down to the people, and he said [this] to them.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
So Moshe went down to the people, and spoke to them.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Moses went down to the people and he said (it) [this warning] to them.



## Chapter 20

###### Exodus 20:1

וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֵ֛ת כׇּל־הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה לֵאמֹֽר׃{ס}

Elohim spoke all these words, saying:


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And God spoke all these words, saying,


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And G-d [Elokim, the Judge, "exacting payment" (for all of the ten commandments, unlike some other sections in the Torah, where performance is rewarded, but non-performance not punished)] spoke all of these things [miraculously, in one utterance (after which He reiterated each commandment individually)] saying, [i.e., the people responding in the affirmative or in the negative as per the nature of the commandment]:


###### Exodus 20:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/20:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/20:2)


אָֽנֹכִ֖י֙ יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֧ר הוֹצֵאתִ֛יךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם מִבֵּ֣֥ית עֲבָדִ֑͏ֽים׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
I am Adonoy, your God, Who brought you out of the land of Egypt, from the house of slaves.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
I am the Lord thy God, who have brought thee out of the land of Miżrayim, out of the house of bondage.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
I am the L-rd your G-d who took you out of the land of Egypt [Having taken you out is sufficient reason that you be subservient to Me.] ("your [singular] G-d") [an opening for Moses to plead for Israel in the episode of the golden calf, viz.: "You said this ("your G-d") to me, not to them!"] from the house of [Pharaoh, to whom you were] servants.


###### Exodus 20:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/20:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/20:3)


לֹֽ֣א־יִהְיֶ֥͏ֽה־לְךָ֛֩ אֱלֹהִ֥֨ים אֲחֵרִ֖֜ים עַל־פָּנָֽ͏ַ֗י׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You must not have any other gods before My Presence.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thou shalt have no other gods beside me.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
There shall not be unto you [(You may not keep them even if you do not make them)] gods of [i.e., made by] others before My presence [i.e., idolatry is interdicted not for this generation alone but eternally (just as I am eternally present)].

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/20:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/20:4)


לֹֽ֣א־תַעֲשֶֽׂ֨ה־לְךָ֥֣ פֶ֣֙סֶל֙׀וְכׇל־תְּמוּנָ֔֡ה אֲשֶׁ֤֣ר בַּשָּׁמַ֣֙יִם֙׀מִמַּ֔֡עַל וַֽאֲשֶׁ֥ר֩ בָּאָ֖֨רֶץ מִתָּ֑͏ַ֜חַת וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּמַּ֖֣יִם**׀** מִתַּ֥֣חַת לָאָֽ֗רֶץ׃

You must not make for yourself any carved image, or picture of anything that is in the heaven above, or on the earth below, or in the water below the earth.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thou shalt not make for thyself any carved idol, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
You shall not make for yourself a graven image or the likeness of anything which is in the heavens above or in the earth below, or in the waters beneath the earth.


###### Exodus 20:5

לֹֽא־תִשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֥֣ה לָהֶ֖ם֮ וְלֹ֣א תׇעׇבְדֵ֑ם֒ כִּ֣י אָֽנֹכִ֞י יְהֹוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ אֵ֣ל קַנָּ֔א פֹּ֠קֵ֠ד עֲוֺ֨ן אָבֹ֧ת עַל־בָּנִ֛ים עַל־שִׁלֵּשִׁ֥ים וְעַל־רִבֵּעִ֖ים לְשֹׂנְאָֽ֑י׃

thou shalt not bow down to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, punishing the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of those that hate me;

You shall not bow down to them and you shall not serve them, for I am the L-rd your G-d, a jealous G-d, ["jealous" to exact punishment, and not "overlooking" idolatry], visiting the sins of the fathers upon the children, for the third and the fourth generations to those who hate Me, [those who perpetuate their fathers' ways],

but showing mercy to thousands of generations of those that love me, and keep my commandments.

You shall not take the name of the L-rd your G-d in vain [by swearing at variance with what is known, e.g., that a pillar of stone is one of gold], for the L-rd will not absolve him who takes His name in vain.

###### Exodus 21:6

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
His master must bring him to the judges. He must then bring him next to the door, or to the doorpost, and his master shall pierce his ear with an awl. He then serves his master forever.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
then his master shall bring him to the judges; he shall also bring him to the door, or to the door post; and his master shall bore his ear through with an awl; and he shall serve him for ever.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
then his master shall bring him near to the judges [(The man-servant must consult the judges who sold him)], and he shall bring him near to the door or to the door-post [(Just as a door-post stands (in its place), so the door (against which his ear is bored) must be standing)], and his master shall bore his [right] ear with an awl, and he shall serve him forever [i.e., until the Jubilee year]. [Why the ear? The ear which heard on Mount Sinai: "Thou shalt not steal!" and he went and stole (for which reason beth-din sold him) — let his ear be bored! Or, if he sold himself: The ear which heard on Mount Sinai: "For unto Me are the children of Israel servants" and he went and acquired a master for himself — let his ear be bored! And why door and door-post? The Holy One Blessed be He said: The door and the door-post, which were witnesses in Egypt when I skipped over the lintel and the two door-posts (on which the Jews had sprinkled the blood of the Paschal lamb), and I said: "For unto Me are the children of Israel servants" — and not servants to servants (i.e., the Egyptians) and this one went and acquired a master for himself! Let his ear (that heard and did not listen) be bored (in their presence!)]

###### Exodus 21:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:14)


וְכִֽי־יָזִ֥ד אִ֛ישׁ עַל־רֵעֵ֖הוּ לְהׇרְג֣וֹ בְעׇרְמָ֑ה מֵעִ֣ם מִזְבְּחִ֔י תִּקָּחֶ֖נּוּ לָמֽוּת׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
But if a man plots against his neighbor to kill him intentionally, you may [even] take him from My altar to put him to death.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
But if a man come presumptuously upon his neighbour, to slay him with guile; thou shalt take him from my altar, that he may die.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if a man be deliberate, [and not unwitting] against his neighbor, [and not against a gentile], to kill him with subtlety [(to exclude a doctor whose patient dies as a result of his treatment, a bailiff of beth-din who kills in the administration of stripes, and one whose son or disciple dies under his chastisement)], from My altar [if he were a Cohein and wished to perform the priestly service] shall you take him to die.


###### Exodus 21:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:15)


וּמַכֵּ֥ה אָבִ֛יו וְאִמּ֖וֹ מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Whoever strikes his father or his mother shall be put to death.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And he that smites his father, or his mother, shall be surely put to death.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if one strikes [and wounds] his father or his mother, he shall be put to death [by strangulation (unlike one who wounds another, who pays but is not killed)].


###### Exodus 21:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:16)


וְגֹנֵ֨ב אִ֧ישׁ וּמְכָר֛וֹ וְנִמְצָ֥א בְיָד֖וֹ מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Whoever steals [kidnaps] a man and sells him, if he is found in his hand, he shall be put to death.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And he that steals a man, and sells him, if he be found in his hand, he shall surely be put to death.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if one, [including a woman, tumtum (one of indeterminate gender) or hermaphrodite], kidnapped a man and sold him, and he were found in his hand, [i.e., men having witnessed his being kidnapped and sold and his having been in the kidnapper's hand before the sale], he (the kidnapper) shall be put to death [by stoning].


###### Exodus 21:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:17)


וּמְקַלֵּ֥ל אָבִ֛יו וְאִמּ֖וֹ מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Whoever curses his father or his mother shall be put to death.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And he that curses his father, or his mother, shall surely be put to death.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if one [including a woman] curses his father or his mother, he shall be put to death [by stoning].


###### Exodus 21:18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:18)


וְכִֽי־יְרִיבֻ֣ן אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְהִכָּה־אִישׁ֙ אֶת־רֵעֵ֔הוּ בְּאֶ֖בֶן א֣וֹ בְאֶגְרֹ֑ף וְלֹ֥א יָמ֖וּת וְנָפַ֥ל לְמִשְׁכָּֽב׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
When men quarrel and one man hits his fellow with a stone or with [his] fist; and he [the victim] does not die but becomes bedridden,


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And if men strive together, and one smite another with a stone, or with his fist, and he die not, but keeps his bed:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if men quarrel and a man strike his neighbor with stone or fist and he not die, but become bedridden [and work-disabled],


###### Exodus 21:19

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:19](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:19)


אִם־יָק֞וּם וְהִתְהַלֵּ֥ךְ בַּח֛וּץ עַל־מִשְׁעַנְתּ֖וֹ וְנִקָּ֣ה הַמַּכֶּ֑ה רַ֥ק שִׁבְתּ֛וֹ יִתֵּ֖ן וְרַפֹּ֥א יְרַפֵּֽא׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If he gets up and is able to walk on the outside on his own power, the one who struck him shall be acquitted. Still he must pay for his loss of work, and must pay for his complete cure.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
if he rise again, and walk abroad upon his staff, then shall he that struck him be acquitted: only he shall pay for the loss of his time, and shall cause him to be thoroughly healed.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If he arise and walk outside on his own power, then the striker shall be absolved [(the striker being imprisoned pending resolution of the victim's state)]; only his work-disability [payment] shall he (the striker) give, and heal shall he heal [i.e., he shall pay medical expenses].


###### Exodus 21:20

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:20](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:20)


וְכִֽי־יַכֶּה֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶת־עַבְדּ֜וֹ א֤וֹ אֶת־אֲמָתוֹ֙ בַּשֵּׁ֔בֶט וּמֵ֖ת תַּ֣חַת יָד֑וֹ נָקֹ֖ם יִנָּקֵֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If a man strikes his male or female slave with a rod, and [the slave] dies under his hand, [the death] must be avenged.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And if a man smite his servant, or his maid, with a rod, and he die under his hand; he shall be surely punished.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if a man strike his [Canaanite] man-servant or maid-servant with a rod [of killing potential], and he die under his hand, vengeance [by the sword] shall be taken.


###### Exodus 21:21

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:21](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:21)


אַ֥ךְ אִם־י֛וֹם א֥וֹ יוֹמַ֖יִם יַעֲמֹ֑ד לֹ֣א יֻקַּ֔ם כִּ֥י כַסְפּ֖וֹ הֽוּא׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
However if he [the slave] survives for a day or two, [his death] is not avenged, for he [the slave] is his [master’s] property.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
But if he continues a day or two, he shall not be punished: for he is his money.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
But if one day or two days [i.e., one day which is like two days, a twenty-four hour period] he survive, vengeance shall not be taken, for he (the man-servant) is his money, [but if another (i.e., not his master) kills him, even if the servant lingered on that long, he (the murderer) is put to death].


###### Exodus 21:22

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:22](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:22)


וְכִֽי־יִנָּצ֣וּ אֲנָשִׁ֗ים וְנָ֨גְפ֜וּ אִשָּׁ֤ה הָרָה֙ וְיָצְא֣וּ יְלָדֶ֔יהָ וְלֹ֥א יִהְיֶ֖ה אָס֑וֹן עָנ֣וֹשׁ יֵעָנֵ֗שׁ כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֨ר יָשִׁ֤ית עָלָיו֙ בַּ֣עַל הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וְנָתַ֖ן בִּפְלִלִֽים׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If men will fight and they strike a pregnant woman, causing her to miscarry, but there is no fatal injury [to the woman], he [the guilty one] is to be punished with a [monetary] penalty when the husband demands compensation. He shall pay as determined by the judges.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If men strive, and hurt a woman with child, so that her fruit depart from her, and yet no further harm ensue: he shall be surely punished, according as the woman’s husband will lay upon him; and he shall pay as the judges determine.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if men fight [with each other and one strikes at the other] and they hit a pregnant woman, and her fetuses miscarry, and there be no death [in the woman], then he shall be punished [i.e., payment (for the fetuses) shall be exacted of him.] As the husband of the woman imposes upon him (the striker) [through beth-din] he shall give by word of the judges.


###### Exodus 21:23

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:23](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:23)


וְאִם־אָס֖וֹן יִהְיֶ֑ה וְנָתַתָּ֥ה נֶ֖פֶשׁ תַּ֥חַת נָֽפֶשׁ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
However if there is a fatal injury, you shall give [up] a life for a life.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
But if any harm ensue, then thou shalt give life for life.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if there be death [in the woman] then you shall give a life for a life [(According to one view, "life," literally; according to another, monetary payment, estimated by the sales-price of servants in the marketplace)].


###### Exodus 21:24

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:24](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:24)


עַ֚יִן תַּ֣חַת עַ֔יִן שֵׁ֖ן תַּ֣חַת שֵׁ֑ן יָ֚ד תַּ֣חַת יָ֔ד רֶ֖גֶל תַּ֥חַת רָֽגֶל׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
[Compensation of] an eye for an eye, [of] a tooth for a tooth, [of] a hand for a hand, [of] a foot for a foot.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
An eye for an eye [(If one blinded another, he pays him the monetary value of an eye, estimated by loss of value of a blinded servant in the marketplace)]; a tooth for a tooth; a hand for a hand; a foot for a foot.


###### Exodus 21:25

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:25](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:25)


כְּוִיָּה֙ תַּ֣חַת כְּוִיָּ֔ה פֶּ֖צַע תַּ֣חַת פָּ֑צַע חַבּוּרָ֕ה תַּ֖חַת חַבּוּרָֽה׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
[Compensation of] a burn for a burn, [of] a wound for a wound, [of] a bruise for a bruise.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
burning for burning, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
A burn [produced by fire] for a burn [(monetary payment, estimated by how much one would give to be spared the pain of the burn)]; a wound [(where blood is drawn)] for a wound [(Though he makes the other payments (loss of limb, disability, etc.,) he is not exempt from payment for pain)]; a welt [(where no blood is drawn)] for a welt.


###### Exodus 21:26

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:26](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:26)


וְכִֽי־יַכֶּ֨ה אִ֜ישׁ אֶת־עֵ֥ין עַבְדּ֛וֹ אֽוֹ־אֶת־עֵ֥ין אֲמָת֖וֹ וְשִֽׁחֲתָ֑הּ לַֽחׇפְשִׁ֥י יְשַׁלְּחֶ֖נּוּ תַּ֥חַת עֵינֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If a man strikes the eye of his slave, or the eye of his female slave, and destroys [blinds] it, he shall set him [the slave] free as compensation for the eye.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And if a man smite the eye of his servant, or the eye of his maid, and destroy it; he shall let him go free for his eye’s sake.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if a man strike the eye of his [Canaanite] man-servant or the eye of his maid-servant, and he destroy it, free shall he send him in lieu of his eye [or any other organ prominences which do not grow back (excluding a child's tooth)].


###### Exodus 21:27

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:27](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:27)


וְאִם־שֵׁ֥ן עַבְדּ֛וֹ אֽוֹ־שֵׁ֥ן אֲמָת֖וֹ יַפִּ֑יל לַֽחׇפְשִׁ֥י יְשַׁלְּחֶ֖נּוּ תַּ֥חַת שִׁנּֽוֹ׃{פ}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If [he knocks out] the tooth of his slave, or knocks out the tooth of his female slave, he shall set him [the slave] free as compensation for the tooth.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And if he strike out his manservant’s tooth, or his maidservant’s tooth; he shall let him go free for his tooth’s sake.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if the tooth [(though one is not born with it, unlike "eye")] of his man-servant or the tooth of his maid-servant he strike out, free shall he send him in lieu of his tooth.


###### Exodus 21:28

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:28](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:28)


וְכִֽי־יִגַּ֨ח שׁ֥וֹר אֶת־אִ֛ישׁ א֥וֹ אֶת־אִשָּׁ֖ה וָמֵ֑ת סָק֨וֹל יִסָּקֵ֜ל הַשּׁ֗וֹר וְלֹ֤א יֵאָכֵל֙ אֶת־בְּשָׂר֔וֹ וּבַ֥עַל הַשּׁ֖וֹר נָקִֽי׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If an ox gores a man or woman and the victim dies, the ox shall be stoned [to death], and its flesh may not be eaten. The owner of the ox shall go unpunished.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If an ox gore a man or a woman, that they die: then the ox shall be surely stoned, and his flesh shall not be eaten; but the owner of the ox shall be acquitted.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if an ox [(or any other animal)] gore a man or a woman and he die, the ox shall be stoned and its flesh shall not be eaten [even if it is slaughtered after judgment has been pronounced upon it], and the owner of the ox is absolved ["the owner" of a tam (an ox that is not "confirmed" in killing, as opposed to a mued, a three-time killer ox. See 29)]


###### Exodus 21:29

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:29](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:29)


וְאִ֡ם שׁוֹר֩ נַגָּ֨ח ה֜וּא מִתְּמֹ֣ל שִׁלְשֹׁ֗ם וְהוּעַ֤ד בִּבְעָלָיו֙ וְלֹ֣א יִשְׁמְרֶ֔נּוּ וְהֵמִ֥ית אִ֖ישׁ א֣וֹ אִשָּׁ֑ה הַשּׁוֹר֙ יִסָּקֵ֔ל וְגַם־בְּעָלָ֖יו יוּמָֽת׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
But if the ox had gored yesterday and the day before, and a warning was given to its owner, but he had not taken proper precautions to guard it, and kills a man or a woman, the ox must be stoned, and the owner also shall die [by Divine decree].


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
But if the ox was wont to gore with his horn in time past, and his owner had been warned, yet he had not kept him in, but it killed a man or a woman; the ox shall be stoned, and its owner also shall be put to death.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if it were a goring ox from yesterday and the day before, [three gorings (including the latest), and the owner were warned [in the presence of witnesses], and he did not guard it, and it killed [(by goring or otherwise)] a man or a woman, the ox shall be stoned, and its owner, too, shall die [at the hands of Heaven].


###### Exodus 21:30

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:30](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:30)


אִם־כֹּ֖פֶר יוּשַׁ֣ת עָלָ֑יו וְנָתַן֙ פִּדְיֹ֣ן נַפְשׁ֔וֹ כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־יוּשַׁ֖ת עָלָֽיו׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
When an atonement fine shall be imposed on him, he must give for the redemption of his soul whatever sum is imposed on him.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If there be laid on him a sum of money, then he shall give for the ransom of his life whatever is laid upon him.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
When kofer ["atonement" (payment)] is set for him, he shall give the redemption of his soul [(According to one view, the value of the victim; according to another, the value of the owner)], according to all that shall be set for him.


###### Exodus 21:31

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:31](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:31)


אוֹ־בֵ֥ן יִגָּ֖ח אוֹ־בַ֣ת יִגָּ֑ח כַּמִּשְׁפָּ֥ט הַזֶּ֖ה יֵעָ֥שֶׂה לּֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Whether it is a son [a minor lad] that is gored or a daughter [a minor girl] that it gored, this law shall apply to it.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Whether he has gored a son, or gored a daughter, according to this judgment shall it be done to him.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Or if it gore a son [a minor], or it gore a daughter [a minor], according to this ordinance shall it be done to him.


###### Exodus 21:32

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:32](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:32)


אִם־עֶ֛בֶד יִגַּ֥ח הַשּׁ֖וֹר א֣וֹ אָמָ֑ה כֶּ֣סֶף**׀** שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שְׁקָלִ֗ים יִתֵּן֙ לַֽאדֹנָ֔יו וְהַשּׁ֖וֹר יִסָּקֵֽל׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If the ox gored a male or female slave, he must give thirty silver shekalim to their master, and the ox must be stoned.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If the ox shall gore a manservant or a maidservant; he shall give to their master thirty shekels of silver, and the ox shall be stoned.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If the ox gore a [Canaanite] man-servant or maid-servant, then silver, thirty shekels, shall he give to his master [regardless of how much he is worth] and the ox shall be stoned.


###### Exodus 21:33

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:33](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:33)


וְכִֽי־יִפְתַּ֨ח אִ֜ישׁ בּ֗וֹר א֠וֹ כִּֽי־יִכְרֶ֥ה אִ֛ישׁ בֹּ֖ר וְלֹ֣א יְכַסֶּ֑נּוּ וְנָֽפַל־שָׁ֥מָּה שּׁ֖וֹר א֥וֹ חֲמֽוֹר׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If a man uncovers a pit, or if a man digs a pit, and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it;


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And if a man shall open a pit, or if a man shall dig a pit, and not cover it, and an ox or an ass fall into it;


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if a man open a pit [(in the public domain) which was covered] or if a man dig a pit [even if he completes another's digging], and he not cover it, and there fall into it an ox or an ass [or any other animal],


###### Exodus 21:34

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:34](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:34)


בַּ֤עַל הַבּוֹר֙ יְשַׁלֵּ֔ם כֶּ֖סֶף יָשִׁ֣יב לִבְעָלָ֑יו וְהַמֵּ֖ת יִֽהְיֶה־לּֽוֹ׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The owner of the pit must pay. He must compensate its owner with money, and the dead [animal] remains his [its original owner’s] possesion.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
the owner of the pit shall make it good, and give money to the owner of them; and the dead beast shall be his.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
the owner of the pit [i.e., the one who occasioned the damage, whether or not he be the actual owner] shall pay. Money shall he restore [(any kind of "restoration," even bran)] to its owner, and the carcass shall belong to him [the latter (as partial payment towards damages)].


###### Exodus 21:35

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:35](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:35)


וְכִֽי־יִגֹּ֧ף שֽׁוֹר־אִ֛ישׁ אֶת־שׁ֥וֹר רֵעֵ֖הוּ וָמֵ֑ת וּמָ֨כְר֜וּ אֶת־הַשּׁ֤וֹר הַחַי֙ וְחָצ֣וּ אֶת־כַּסְפּ֔וֹ וְגַ֥ם אֶת־הַמֵּ֖ת יֶֽחֱצֽוּן׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If a man’s ox injures his neighbor’s ox and it dies, they shall sell the live ox and divide the money received for it. They shall also divide [the value of] the dead animal.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And if one man’s ox hurt another’s, that he die; then they shall sell the live ox, and divide the money of it; and the dead ox also they shall divide.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if the ox [a tam ("non-confirmed" in damaging)] of a man strike [(any kind of "striking" — butting, kicking, biting, etc.)] the ox of his neighbor, and it die, then they shall sell the living ox and halve its money [between them] and also the [value of the] carcass shall they halve [between them (so that the owner of the tam, where both oxen are of equal value, pays half-damages)].


###### Exodus 21:36

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:36](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:36)


א֣וֹ נוֹדַ֗ע כִּ֠י שׁ֣וֹר נַגָּ֥ח הוּא֙ מִתְּמ֣וֹל שִׁלְשֹׁ֔ם וְלֹ֥א יִשְׁמְרֶ֖נּוּ בְּעָלָ֑יו שַׁלֵּ֨ם יְשַׁלֵּ֥ם שׁוֹר֙ תַּ֣חַת הַשּׁ֔וֹר וְהַמֵּ֖ת יִֽהְיֶה־לּֽוֹ׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If it was known that it was a goring ox from yesterday and the day before, but he had not taken proper precaution to guard it, then he must pay full compensation, an ox for an ox. The dead [animal] remains in the possession [of its owner].


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Or if it be known that the ox has long been in the habit of goring, and his owner has not kept him in; he shall surely pay ox for ox; and the dead shall be his own.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Or [if it were not a tam, but] it be known that it were a goring ox [a mued] from yesterday and the day before, [three gorings (including the latest)], and its owner did not guard it, then pay shall he pay, an ox [full value] for an ox, and the carcass shall belong to him [the owner of the gored ox, (the owner of the goring ox making up the difference between the value of the carcass and the full value of the gored ox)].


###### Exodus 21:37

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:37](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:37)


כִּ֤י יִגְנֹֽב־אִישׁ֙ שׁ֣וֹר אוֹ־שֶׂ֔ה וּטְבָח֖וֹ א֣וֹ מְכָר֑וֹ חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה בָקָ֗ר יְשַׁלֵּם֙ תַּ֣חַת הַשּׁ֔וֹר וְאַרְבַּע־צֹ֖אן תַּ֥חַת הַשֶּֽׂה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If a man steals an ox or a sheep, and then slaughters or sells it, he must pay five oxen for each ox, and four sheep for each sheep.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If a man shall steal an ox, or a sheep, and kill it, or sell it; he shall restore five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If a man steal an ox or a lamb, and slaughter it or sell it, then five (head of) cattle shall he pay for the ox, and four sheep for the lamb, ["ox" and "lamb," specifically (Only four for the lamb, as opposed to five for the ox, for the thief suffers shame in carrying the lamb (whereas he leads the ox)].



## Chapter 22

###### Exodus 22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:1)


אִם־בַּמַּחְתֶּ֛רֶת יִמָּצֵ֥א הַגַּנָּ֖ב וְהֻכָּ֣ה וָמֵ֑ת אֵ֥ין ל֖וֹ דָּמִֽים׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If the thief is found [caught] while breaking in, and is struck and killed, there is no liability for his blood.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If a thief be found breaking in, and be smitten that he die, there shall no blood be shed on his account.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If the thief be found breaking in, and he be struck (by the owner) and die, he (the owner) has no blood [liability, the thief coming with intent to kill the owner if necessary, and "If one comes to kill you, arise and kill him!"]


###### Exodus 22:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:2)


אִם־זָרְחָ֥ה הַשֶּׁ֛מֶשׁ עָלָ֖יו דָּמִ֣ים ל֑וֹ שַׁלֵּ֣ם יְשַׁלֵּ֔ם אִם־אֵ֣ין ל֔וֹ וְנִמְכַּ֖ר בִּגְנֵבָתֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If the sun shone on him, there is liability for his blood. He must make full restitution. If he does not have [the means to do so], he shall be sold [as a slave to pay] for his theft.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If the sun be risen upon him, there shall be blood shed on his account. He should make full restitution; if he have nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If the sun shone upon him [i.e., If it is obvious that the thief would not kill him (as in the instance of a father stealing from a son)], he (the thief) "has blood" [i.e., he is regarded as a "live man," and one who kills him is a murderer.] Pay shall he [the thief] pay [for what he stole (but he is not to be put to death)]. If he lacks it, he is to be sold for his theft.


###### Exodus 22:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:3)


אִֽם־הִמָּצֵא֩ תִמָּצֵ֨א בְיָד֜וֹ הַגְּנֵבָ֗ה מִשּׁ֧וֹר עַד־חֲמ֛וֹר עַד־שֶׂ֖ה חַיִּ֑ים שְׁנַ֖יִם יְשַׁלֵּֽם׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If the stolen article is found in his hand [possession], whether it is an ox, donkey or sheep, he must pay two live animals.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If the theft be at all found in his hand alive, whether it be ox, or ass, or sheep; he shall restore double.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If the theft be found in his hand [i.e., in his possession, he neither having slaughtered it nor sold it], from ox to ass, to lamb [(all objects are included)], living (animals) [or their value, and not dead animals], double shall he pay.


###### Exodus 22:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:4)


כִּ֤י יַבְעֶר־אִישׁ֙ שָׂדֶ֣ה אוֹ־כֶ֔רֶם וְשִׁלַּח֙ אֶת־בְּעִירֹ֔ה וּבִעֵ֖ר בִּשְׂדֵ֣ה אַחֵ֑ר מֵיטַ֥ב שָׂדֵ֛הוּ וּמֵיטַ֥ב כַּרְמ֖וֹ יְשַׁלֵּֽם׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If he damages a field or vineyard with his animal—he lets his livestock loose, and [or] it feeds in another’s field—from his [own] prime field and prime vineyard he must compensate [the owner].


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If a man shall cause a field or vineyard to be eaten, and shall put in his beast, and shall feed in another man’s field; of the best of his field, and of the best of his vineyard, shall he make restitution


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If a man take his beast into a field or a vineyard and he send his beast [and it tread, causing damage] or ravage [by the "tooth"] in the field of another, then the best of his (the animal owner's) field and the best of his vineyard shall he pay [if he wishes to pay him in land].


###### Exodus 22:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:5)


כִּֽי־תֵצֵ֨א אֵ֜שׁ וּמָצְאָ֤ה קֹצִים֙ וְנֶאֱכַ֣ל גָּדִ֔ישׁ א֥וֹ הַקָּמָ֖ה א֣וֹ הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה שַׁלֵּ֣ם יְשַׁלֵּ֔ם הַמַּבְעִ֖ר אֶת־הַבְּעֵרָֽה׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If a fire goes out of control and finds [catches on] thorns, and then consumes bound or standing grain or a field, full restitution must be made by the one who started the fire.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If fire break out, and catch in thorns, so that the sheaves, or the standing corn, or the field, be consumed; he that kindled the fire shall surely make restitution.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If fire go out [even of itself] and it find thorns, and there be consumed [by the progress of the fire in the thorns] sheaves, or the standing corn, or the field, [his furrow being singed so that it has to be re-plowed], pay shall he pay, he that lights the fire [even though he lights it in his own property and it moves of itself by means of the thorns].


###### Exodus 22:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:6)


כִּֽי־יִתֵּן֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵ֜הוּ כֶּ֤סֶף אֽוֹ־כֵלִים֙ לִשְׁמֹ֔ר וְגֻנַּ֖ב מִבֵּ֣ית הָאִ֑ישׁ אִם־יִמָּצֵ֥א הַגַּנָּ֖ב יְשַׁלֵּ֥ם שְׁנָֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If a man gives his neighbor money or articles to safeguard and they are stolen from the house of the [watch]man, if the thief is found, he must pay double.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If a man shall deliver to his neighbour money or vessels to keep, and it be stolen out of the man’s house; if the thief be found, he shall pay double.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If a man give to his neighbor money or vessels to watch [without pay], and it be stolen from the house of the man [(this being the latter's claim)], if the thief is found, he shall pay double [to the owner].


###### Exodus 22:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:7)


אִם־לֹ֤א יִמָּצֵא֙ הַגַּנָּ֔ב וְנִקְרַ֥ב בַּֽעַל־הַבַּ֖יִת אֶל־הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים אִם־לֹ֥א שָׁלַ֛ח יָד֖וֹ בִּמְלֶ֥אכֶת רֵעֵֽהוּ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If the thief is not found, the owner of the house [the watchman] must come before the judges [Beis Din], [to swear] that he did not lay a hand on his neighbor’s possessions [for his personal use].


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If the thief be not found, then the master of the house shall be brought to the judges, to swear that he has not put his hand to his neighbour’s goods.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If the thief not be found, then the master of the house [where the article had been deposited] shall draw near to the judges [to deliberate with the owner and to swear to him] that he has not sent his hand against his neighbor's deposit.


###### Exodus 22:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:8)


עַֽל־כׇּל־דְּבַר־פֶּ֡שַׁע עַל־שׁ֡וֹר עַל־חֲ֠מ֠וֹר עַל־שֶׂ֨ה עַל־שַׂלְמָ֜ה עַל־כׇּל־אֲבֵדָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר יֹאמַר֙ כִּי־ה֣וּא זֶ֔ה עַ֚ד הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים יָבֹ֖א דְּבַר־שְׁנֵיהֶ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר יַרְשִׁיעֻן֙ אֱלֹהִ֔ים יְשַׁלֵּ֥ם שְׁנַ֖יִם לְרֵעֵֽהוּ׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
In every question of dishonesty whether it involves an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or anything that was [allegedly] lost of which [a witness] says, “This is it!” the claims of both parties must be brought to the judges. The one whom the judges find guilty, must pay double restitution to his neighbor.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
For all manner of trespass, whether it be for ox, for ass, for sheep, for a garment, or for any manner of lost thing, of which one can say, This is it, the cause of both parties shall come before the judges; and whom the judges shall condemn, he shall pay double to his neighbour.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For every matter of offense, [where he is found to have lied under oath, witnesses testifying that he himself stole it, and the judges incriminating him on their testimony], for an ox, for an ass, for a lamb, for a garment, for every lost object about which he [the witness] will say that it is this [whereunto you swore that it was stolen, and, behold, you have it], unto the judges, [who shall cross-examine the witnesses,] shall come the matter of both, [and] whom the judges shall incriminate [i.e., the watcher, if he is found guilty], shall pay double to his neighbor.


###### Exodus 22:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:9)


כִּֽי־יִתֵּן֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵ֜הוּ חֲמ֨וֹר אוֹ־שׁ֥וֹר אוֹ־שֶׂ֛ה וְכׇל־בְּהֵמָ֖ה לִשְׁמֹ֑ר וּמֵ֛ת אוֹ־נִשְׁבַּ֥ר אוֹ־נִשְׁבָּ֖ה אֵ֥ין רֹאֶֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If a man gives his neighbor, a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any animal for safeguarding; and it dies, or is injured, or is captured, and there is no eyewitness,


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If a man deliver to his neighbour an ass, or an ox, or a sheep, or any beast, to keep; and it die, or be hurt, or be driven away, no man seeing it:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If a man give to his neighbor an ass or an ox or a lamb or any beast to watch [for pay], and it die [naturally] or be broken or seized [by robbers], no one seeing [to testify to this],


###### Exodus 22:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:10)


שְׁבֻעַ֣ת יְהֹוָ֗ה תִּהְיֶה֙ בֵּ֣ין שְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם אִם־לֹ֥א שָׁלַ֛ח יָד֖וֹ בִּמְלֶ֣אכֶת רֵעֵ֑הוּ וְלָקַ֥ח בְּעָלָ֖יו וְלֹ֥א יְשַׁלֵּֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
an oath to Adonoy shall be between them, that he [the watcher] did not lay his hand on his neighbor’s possession [for his personal use]. The owner must accept it [the oath], and [the watcher] need not make restitution.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
then shall an oath of the Lord be between them both, that he has not put his hand to his neighbour’s goods; and the owner of it shall accept this, and he shall not make it good.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
the oath of the L-rd shall be between both, that he (the watcher) did not send his hand against the deposit of his neighbor [to use it for himself (for if he did, and it afterwards met with mischance, he is liable)], and its owner shall accept [the oath], and he [the watcher] shall not pay.


###### Exodus 22:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:11)


וְאִם־גָּנֹ֥ב יִגָּנֵ֖ב מֵעִמּ֑וֹ יְשַׁלֵּ֖ם לִבְעָלָֽיו׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
But if it was indeed stolen from him, he must make restitution to its owner.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
But if it be stolen from him, he shall make restitution to its owner.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if it were stolen from him, he shall pay its owner.


###### Exodus 22:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:12)


אִם־טָרֹ֥ף יִטָּרֵ֖ף יְבִאֵ֣הוּ עֵ֑ד הַטְּרֵפָ֖ה לֹ֥א יְשַׁלֵּֽם׃{פ}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If it was torn apart [killed by wild beasts], he [the watcher] must provide witnesses. He then need not pay for that which was torn apart.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If it be torn in pieces, then let him bring it as evidence; he shall not make good that which was torn.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If it were torn [by a wild beast], let him bring witnesses [to that effect and thereby free himself of liability]. For the torn (beast) [(which he could not save, as when it was torn by a lion)] he shall not pay.


###### Exodus 22:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:13)


וְכִֽי־יִשְׁאַ֥ל אִ֛ישׁ מֵעִ֥ם רֵעֵ֖הוּ וְנִשְׁבַּ֣ר אוֹ־מֵ֑ת בְּעָלָ֥יו אֵין־עִמּ֖וֹ שַׁלֵּ֥ם יְשַׁלֵּֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If a man borrows something from his neighbor, and it becomes broken or dies; if the owner is not [involved] with him, he [the borrower] must make full restitution.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And if a man borrow aught of his neighbour, and it be hurt, or die, its owner not being with it, he shall surely make it good.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if a man borrow from his neighbor and it be broken or die, its owner not being with (i.e., engaged by) him [the borrower, in his work], pay shall he (the borrower) pay.


###### Exodus 22:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:14)


אִם־בְּעָלָ֥יו עִמּ֖וֹ לֹ֣א יְשַׁלֵּ֑ם אִם־שָׂכִ֣יר ה֔וּא בָּ֖א בִּשְׂכָרֽוֹ׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If the owner is [involved] with him, then he [the borrower] need not make restitution. If it was hired, it [the ox] comes in its rental price.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
But if its owner be with it, he shall not make it good: if it be a hired thing, it came for his hire.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If its owner were with him [whether in the same work (as the animal) or some other work, even if he were not with him at the time of breaking or death], he (the borrower) shall not pay. If it (the animal) were hired, it came by its hire [into the hands of the hirer, who, paying for it, (unlike the borrower), is not liable for mischance. (There is a difference of opinion as to whether he is to be regarded as an unpaid watcher or as a paid one.)]


###### Exodus 22:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:15)


וְכִֽי־יְפַתֶּ֣ה אִ֗ישׁ בְּתוּלָ֛ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־אֹרָ֖שָׂה וְשָׁכַ֣ב עִמָּ֑הּ מָהֹ֛ר יִמְהָרֶ֥נָּה לּ֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If a man seduces a virgin who is not betrothed, and lies with her; he must give the dowry to acquire her as his wife.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And if a man seduce a virgin that is not betrothed, and lie with her, he shall pay the bride price for her to be his wife.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if a man entice a virgin who is not betrothed and he lie with her, he shall endower her unto himself as a wife [i.e., he shall write her a kethubah (a marriage contract) and marry her.]


###### Exodus 22:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:16)


אִם־מָאֵ֧ן יְמָאֵ֛ן אָבִ֖יהָ לְתִתָּ֣הּ ל֑וֹ כֶּ֣סֶף יִשְׁקֹ֔ל כְּמֹ֖הַר הַבְּתוּלֹֽת׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If her father utterly refuses to give her to him, he must give [the father] the weight of silver equal to the dowry usually given to virgins.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If her father utterly refuse to give her to him, he shall pay money according to the marriage price of virgins.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If her father refuse to give her to him, money shall he pay [fifty shekels] as per the indemnity for the [ravished] virgins (see Deuteronomy 22:29)].


###### Exodus 22:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:17)


מְכַשֵּׁפָ֖ה לֹ֥א תְחַיֶּֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You shall not allow a witch to live.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
A witch you shall not allow to live, [but you shall kill her, or him, as the case may be, (in beth-din)].


###### Exodus 22:18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:18)


כׇּל־שֹׁכֵ֥ב עִם־בְּהֵמָ֖ה מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Whoever lies with an animal must be put to death.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Whoever cohabits with a beast shall surely be put to death.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Anyone who lies with a beast [either actively or passively] shall be put to death [by stoning].


###### Exodus 22:19

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:19](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:19)


זֹבֵ֥חַ לָאֱלֹהִ֖ים יׇֽחֳרָ֑ם בִּלְתִּ֥י לַיהֹוָ֖ה לְבַדּֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Whoever slaughters to a god must be condemned [to die]. [Sacrifices may be offered] to Adonoy alone.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
He that sacrifices to any god, save to the Lord only, he shall be utterly destroyed.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
One who slaughters [(or performs any inner Temple service, like slaughtering) to idolatry shall be put to death — only to the L-rd alone!


###### Exodus 22:20

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:20](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:20)


וְגֵ֥ר לֹא־תוֹנֶ֖ה וְלֹ֣א תִלְחָצֶ֑נּוּ כִּֽי־גֵרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You must not abuse or oppress a stranger, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thou shalt neither vex a stranger, nor oppress him: for you were strangers in the land of Miżrayim.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And a stranger [from another land] you shall not taunt and you shall not oppress him [by theft], for you were strangers in the land of Egypt [and are equally vulnerable to taunting].


###### Exodus 22:21

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:21](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:21)


כׇּל־אַלְמָנָ֥ה וְיָת֖וֹם לֹ֥א תְעַנּֽוּן׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You must not mistreat any widow or orphan.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
You shall not afflict any widow, or fatherless child.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Every widow and orphan you shall not afflict. [All men are intended; it is just that "widow and orphan" are more vulnerable to affliction.]


###### Exodus 22:22

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:22](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:22)


אִם־עַנֵּ֥ה תְעַנֶּ֖ה אֹת֑וֹ כִּ֣י אִם־צָעֹ֤ק יִצְעַק֙ אֵלַ֔י שָׁמֹ֥עַ אֶשְׁמַ֖ע צַעֲקָתֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If you do mistreat him [them], when he cries out to Me, I will indeed hear his cry.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If thou at all afflict them, and they cry to me, I will surely hear their cry;


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If you afflict him, [you will receive your just deserts]; for if he but cry out to Me, I will hear his cry.


###### Exodus 22:23

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:23](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:23)


וְחָרָ֣ה אַפִּ֔י וְהָרַגְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם בֶּחָ֑רֶב וְהָי֤וּ נְשֵׁיכֶם֙ אַלְמָנ֔וֹת וּבְנֵיכֶ֖ם יְתֹמִֽים׃{פ}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Then I will cause My anger to flare, and I will kill you by the sword. Your wives will become widows and your children will be orphans.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and my anger shall be inflamed, and I will kill you with the sword; then your wives shall be widows, and your children fatherless.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And My wrath shall burn and I shall kill you by the sword, and your wives will be widows, and your children, orphans [There will be no witnesses to your death, and your wives will not be able to remarry or your sons to inherit you.]


###### Exodus 22:24

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:24](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:24)


אִם־כֶּ֣סֶף**׀** תַּלְוֶ֣ה אֶת־עַמִּ֗י אֶת־הֶֽעָנִי֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ לֹא־תִהְיֶ֥ה ל֖וֹ כְּנֹשֶׁ֑ה לֹֽא־תְשִׂימ֥וּן עָלָ֖יו נֶֽשֶׁךְ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
When you lend money to My people, to the poor person who is with [among] you, do not act toward him as a [demanding] creditor. Do not place the burden of interest upon him.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If thou lend money to any of my people that is poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as a creditor, neither shall you lay upon him interest.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
When you lend money, [lend it, preferentially, in this order:] My people [before heathens], the poor man [before the relatively wealthier] with you [in your city, before the poor of other cities]. Do not be to him as a creditor [Do not be severe in demanding payment. If you know that he is without means, act towards him as if you had not lent him.] Do not impose interest (neshech) upon him, [neshech — "biting." Interest is like the biting of a snake. It begins with an almost imperceptible wound and then "swells" up to one's head.]


###### Exodus 22:25

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:25](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:25)


אִם־חָבֹ֥ל תַּחְבֹּ֖ל שַׂלְמַ֣ת רֵעֶ֑ךָ עַד־בֹּ֥א הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ תְּשִׁיבֶ֥נּוּ לֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If you take your neighbor’s garment as security, you must return it to him till sunset;


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If thou at all take thy neighbour’s garment for a pledge, thou shalt deliver it to him by sundown:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If you take as a pledge the garment of your neighbor [after the time for repayment of the loan arrives and he does not pay], until the setting of the sun return it to him. [Scripture here speaks of a day garment, which is not needed at night. (Restore it for the day and you may take it again at night.)]


###### Exodus 22:26

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:26](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:26)


כִּ֣י הִ֤וא כְסוּתֹה֙ לְבַדָּ֔הּ הִ֥וא שִׂמְלָת֖וֹ לְעֹר֑וֹ בַּמֶּ֣ה יִשְׁכָּ֔ב וְהָיָה֙ כִּֽי־יִצְעַ֣ק אֵלַ֔י וְשָׁמַעְתִּ֖י כִּֽי־חַנּ֥וּן אָֽנִי׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
For this alone is his covering, the garment [to cover] his skin. With what shall he lie down [to sleep]? If it happens that he cries out to Me, I will hear [his cry] for I am gracious.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
for that is his only covering, it is his garment for his skin: in what shall he sleep? and it shall come to pass, when he cries to me, that I will hear; for I am gracious.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For it is his solitary covering, [his outer garment]; it is his shirt for his skin [his inner garment]. On what shall he lie? [This includes his couch (as having to be returned for the day.)] And it shall be, if he cries out to Me, I shall hear; for I am gracious.


###### Exodus 22:27

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:27](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:27)


אֱלֹהִ֖ים לֹ֣א תְקַלֵּ֑ל וְנָשִׂ֥יא בְעַמְּךָ֖ לֹ֥א תָאֹֽר׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Do not curse judges. Do not curse a leader of your people.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thou shalt not revile the judges, nor curse the ruler of thy people.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Elohim you shall not curse [(an exhortation against cursing G-d and against cursing a judge)], and a prince in your people you shall not curse.


###### Exodus 22:28

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:28](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:28)


מְלֵאָתְךָ֥ וְדִמְעֲךָ֖ לֹ֣א תְאַחֵ֑ר בְּכ֥וֹר בָּנֶ֖יךָ תִּתֶּן־לִֽי׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
[Your offering of] the fullness [of your newly ripened produce] and of your terumah-offering’s you must not delay. The first-born of your sons, you shall give to Me.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thou shalt not delay to offer the first of thy ripe fruits, and of thy liquors: the firstborn of thy sons shalt thou give to me.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Your fullness [the obligation that is incumbent upon you when your produce has fully ripened, i.e., bikkurim (first fruits)] and your dema (terumah) you shall not delay [you are not to change the order of their separation. You are not to take terumah before bikkurim or ma'aser before terumah]. The first-born of your sons you shall give to Me [(Redeem him from the Cohein for five sela'im)].


###### Exodus 22:29

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:29](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:29)


כֵּֽן־תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה לְשֹׁרְךָ֖ לְצֹאנֶ֑ךָ שִׁבְעַ֤ת יָמִים֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה עִם־אִמּ֔וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁמִינִ֖י תִּתְּנוֹ־לִֽי׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You must do likewise with your oxen and with your sheep. Seven days it shall remain with its mother. On the eighth day you must give it to Me.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
In like manner shalt thou do with thy oxen, and with thy sheep: seven days it shall be with his dam; on the eighth day thou shalt give it me.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Thus shall you do with your ox, with your sheep [i.e., Just as a human bechor is redeemed after thirty days, so the bechor of small cattle (e.g., sheep) is to be looked after for thirty days and then given to the Cohein.] Seven days shall it be with its mother [(an exhortation to the Cohein not to sacrifice it before the eighth day)]; on the eighth day you may give it to Me.


###### Exodus 22:30

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:30](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:30)


וְאַנְשֵׁי־קֹ֖דֶשׁ תִּהְי֣וּן לִ֑י וּבָשָׂ֨ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֤ה טְרֵפָה֙ לֹ֣א תֹאכֵ֔לוּ לַכֶּ֖לֶב תַּשְׁלִכ֥וּן אֹתֽוֹ׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You shall be men of holiness to Me, and you must not eat flesh that was torn off in the field. Throw it to the dog.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And you shall be holy men to me: neither shall you eat any meat that is torn of beasts in the field; you shall cast it to the dogs.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And [if] men of holiness [i.e., If you separate yourselves from abominations of neveilah and treifah], you shall be unto Me [i.e., you shall be Mine; if not, you shall not be Mine.] And flesh torn [by a predatory animal from a live clean animal] in the field [(not necessarily the field, "the field" being the common instance)] you shall not eat; to the dog you shall throw it [or you may sell it to a heathen ("the dog" being mentioned to indicate that it takes precedence to selling and also that "the Holy One Blessed be He does not withhold the reward of any creature" (see 11:7)].



## Chapter 23

###### Exodus 23:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:1)


לֹ֥א תִשָּׂ֖א שֵׁ֣מַע שָׁ֑וְא אַל־תָּ֤שֶׁת יָֽדְךָ֙ עִם־רָשָׁ֔ע לִהְיֹ֖ת עֵ֥ד חָמָֽס׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Do not accept a false report. Do not join hands with a wicked man to be a corrupt [false] witness.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thou shalt not raise a false report: put not thy hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Do not bear a false report [(an exhortation against receiving slander and an exhortation to a judge not to hear the words of one litigant before the other arrives)]. Do not place your hand with an evildoer [who puts forth a false claim against his neighbor] to [promise him to] be a false witness [for him].


###### Exodus 23:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:2)


לֹֽא־תִהְיֶ֥ה אַחֲרֵֽי־רַבִּ֖ים לְרָעֹ֑ת וְלֹא־תַעֲנֶ֣ה עַל־רִ֗ב לִנְטֹ֛ת אַחֲרֵ֥י רַבִּ֖ים לְהַטֹּֽת׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Do not follow the majority to do evil. Do not respond with your opinion in a dispute [merely] to lean [toward one side]. It must be decided by the majority.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil; neither shalt thou speak in a cause to incline after a multitude to pervert justice:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Do not incline [in judgment] after many [wicked men, simply because they are many] for evil. And do not answer [the defendant, who solicits your judgment] in the dispute, to incline after [those] many [wicked ones] to incline [the judgment from the truth; but judge in accordance with the truth and "let the collar (of responsibility) hang on the neck of the many"].


###### Exodus 23:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:3)


וְדָ֕ל לֹ֥א תֶהְדַּ֖ר בְּרִיבֽוֹ׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Do not show favor [even] to the poor in his dispute.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
nor shalt thou favour a poor man in his cause.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And do not honor a poor man in his quarrel [to favor him in judgment simply because he is poor].


###### Exodus 23:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:4)


כִּ֣י תִפְגַּ֞ע שׁ֧וֹר אֹֽיִבְךָ֛ א֥וֹ חֲמֹר֖וֹ תֹּעֶ֑ה הָשֵׁ֥ב תְּשִׁיבֶ֖נּוּ לֽוֹ׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If you come across your enemy’s ox or his donkey going astray, bring it back to him.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If thou meet thy enemy’s ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If you encounter the ox of your foe, or his ass, straying, return shall you return it to him.


###### Exodus 23:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:5)


כִּֽי־תִרְאֶ֞ה חֲמ֣וֹר שֹׂנַאֲךָ֗ רֹבֵץ֙ תַּ֣חַת מַשָּׂא֔וֹ וְחָדַלְתָּ֖ מֵעֲזֹ֣ב ל֑וֹ עָזֹ֥ב תַּעֲזֹ֖ב עִמּֽוֹ׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If you see the donkey of your enemy lying under its burden, and you might not want to help him, [but you should] make every effort to help him.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If thou see the ass of him that hates thee lying under its burden, and wouldst forbear to unload it, thou shalt surely unload it with him.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Would you see the ass of your foe lying under its burden and forbear to help [disburden] it? Help shall you help [unload it] with him [the owner].


###### Exodus 23:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:6)


לֹ֥א תַטֶּ֛ה מִשְׁפַּ֥ט אֶבְיֹנְךָ֖ בְּרִיבֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Do not bend justice [even] for your needy in his dispute.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thou shalt not pervert the judgment of thy poor in his cause.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Do not incline the judgment of your needy one in his quarrel.


###### Exodus 23:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:7)


מִדְּבַר־שֶׁ֖קֶר תִּרְחָ֑ק וְנָקִ֤י וְצַדִּיק֙ אַֽל־תַּהֲרֹ֔ג כִּ֥י לֹא־אַצְדִּ֖יק רָשָֽׁע׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Keep far away from anything false. Do not kill an innocent righteous man, for I will not acquit a wicked person.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Keep thee far from a false matter; and the innocent and righteous slay thou not: for I will not justify the wicked.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
From a thing of falsehood keep far, and a clean one and a righteous one you shall not kill [("a clean one": If you have something to say in his favor after he has been sentenced to death, the case is to be reopened. "a righteous one": If you have something to say against him after he has been acquitted (i.e., found "righteous") the case is not to be re-opened)], for I will not find the wicked one righteous [(so that even if he has been erroneously acquitted, "the L-rd has many messengers")].


###### Exodus 23:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:8)


וְשֹׁ֖חַד לֹ֣א תִקָּ֑ח כִּ֤י הַשֹּׁ֙חַד֙ יְעַוֵּ֣ר פִּקְחִ֔ים וִֽיסַלֵּ֖ף דִּבְרֵ֥י צַדִּיקִֽים׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Do not accept bribery, for bribery blinds the clear-sighted, and perverts the words of justice.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt take no bribe: for the bribe blinds the wise, and perverts the words of the righteous.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And a bribe you shall not take [even to judge truly], for a bribe blinds the wise and undermines righteous words [i.e., true judgments].


###### Exodus 23:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:9)


וְגֵ֖ר לֹ֣א תִלְחָ֑ץ וְאַתֶּ֗ם יְדַעְתֶּם֙ אֶת־נֶ֣פֶשׁ הַגֵּ֔ר כִּֽי־גֵרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Do not oppress a stranger. You [should] know the soul [feelings] of the stranger, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Also thou shalt not oppress a stranger: for you know the heart of a stranger, seeing you were strangers in the land of Miżrayim.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And a stranger you shall not oppress. And you have known the soul of the stranger [how he suffers under oppression], for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.


###### Exodus 23:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:10)


וְשֵׁ֥שׁ שָׁנִ֖ים תִּזְרַ֣ע אֶת־אַרְצֶ֑ךָ וְאָסַפְתָּ֖ אֶת־תְּבוּאָתָֽהּ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You may sow your land for six years, and gather its crops.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And six years thou shalt sow thy land, and shalt gather in its fruits:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And six years shall you sow your land and you shall gather [into your house] its produce.


###### Exodus 23:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:11)


וְהַשְּׁבִיעִ֞ת תִּשְׁמְטֶ֣נָּה וּנְטַשְׁתָּ֗הּ וְאָֽכְלוּ֙ אֶבְיֹנֵ֣י עַמֶּ֔ךָ וְיִתְרָ֕ם תֹּאכַ֖ל חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה כֵּֽן־תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה לְכַרְמְךָ֖ לְזֵיתֶֽךָ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
But on the seventh [year] you must let it rest, and abandon it [by not eating its produce], and let the needy among your people eat it. What they leave over, the beasts of the field can eat. Do the same with your vineyard and your olive [trees].


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
but the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie fallow; that the poor of thy people may eat: and what they leave, the beasts of the field shall eat. In like manner thou shalt deal with thy vineyard, and with thy olive grove.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the seventh year it shall lie fallow [and not be worked] and you shall leave it [i.e., you shall not eat of its produce after the time of removal (see Leviticus 25:7)], and the poor of your people shall eat it, and what they leave shall be eaten by the animals of the field [(Just as it need not be tithed for animals, so it need not be tithed for the poor — whence it is derived that ma'aser does not obtain in the sabbatical year)]. Thus shall you [also] do with your vineyard and with your olive grove, [(what precedes applying to a grain field)].


###### Exodus 23:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:12)


שֵׁ֤שֶׁת יָמִים֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה מַעֲשֶׂ֔יךָ וּבַיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖י תִּשְׁבֹּ֑ת לְמַ֣עַן יָנ֗וּחַ שֽׁוֹרְךָ֙ וַחֲמֹרֶ֔ךָ וְיִנָּפֵ֥שׁ בֶּן־אֲמָתְךָ֖ וְהַגֵּֽר׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You may do your work six days, but on the seventh day you must cease; so that your ox and your donkey may rest, and the son of your female slave may be refreshed, and [also] the stranger.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Six days thou shalt do thy work, and on the seventh day thou shalt rest: that thy ox and thy ass may rest; and the son of thy handmaid, and the stranger, may be refreshed.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Six days shall you do your work, and on the seventh day shall you rest [i.e., Shabbath is not superseded by Shevi'ith (which is also a commemoration of the creation)], so that there rest your ox and your ass [Give it "resting," i.e., allow it to tear grass from the earth and eat it], and there be refreshed the son of your maidservant [an uncircumcised Canaanite servant] and the stranger [a ger toshav, a "sojourning stranger" (one who shuns idolatry and observes the seven Noachide laws)].


###### Exodus 23:13

Preserve everything that I have said to you. Do not mention the name of other gods. You must not cause it to be heard through your mouth.

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And all that I have spoken to you, you shall observe [(all positive commandments are hereby "affixed" with an exhortation)]. And the name of other gods you shall not mention [One should not say to another: "Wait for me near that idol" (mentioning its name) or "Stand with me on the festival of that idol"]; it shall not be heard [from the gentile] upon your mouth [i.e., at your instigation. (Do not enter into partnership with a gentile, lest he swear by his god (in the instance of a dispute) in which instance you are an accessory to the mentioning of idolatry.)]

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Three times a year you are to celebrate with Me.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Three times shall you celebrate for Me in the year.


###### Exodus 23:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:15)


אֶת־חַ֣ג הַמַּצּוֹת֮ תִּשְׁמֹר֒ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִים֩ תֹּאכַ֨ל מַצּ֜וֹת כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֗ךָ לְמוֹעֵד֙ חֹ֣דֶשׁ הָֽאָבִ֔יב כִּי־ב֖וֹ יָצָ֣אתָ מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וְלֹא־יֵרָא֥וּ פָנַ֖י רֵיקָֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You must keep the festival of Matzos. You must eat matzos for seven days, as I have commanded you. [This festival must be celebrated] at the appointed time, during the month when the grain is ripened, for in it [at this time] you went out of Egypt. Do not appear before My Presence empty-handed.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thou shalt keep the feast of unleavened bread: (thou shalt eat unleavened bread seven days, as I commanded thee, in the time appointed of the month Aviv; for in it thou didst come out from Miżrayim: and none shall appear before me empty:)


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The festival of matzoth shall you keep. Seven days shall you eat matzoth, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of aviv, [when the grain begins to ripen]; for in it did you go out of Egypt. And they shall not appear before Me empty-handed, [but they shall bring burnt-offerings].


###### Exodus 23:16

[You must also keep] the Festival of Harvest, [with bringing bikurim] the first fruits of your labor, which you planted in the field; [also] the Festival of Ingathering, at the close of the year, when you gather in [the fruits of] your labor from the field.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and the feast of harvest, the firstfruits of thy labours, which thou hast sown in the field: and the feast of ingathering, which is at the end of the year, when thou hast gathered in thy labours out of the field.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the festival of the harvest [Shavuoth], the [time of bringing the] first-fruits of your labor, which you sow in the field [(the two loaves of Shavuoth permitting the new wheat for meal-offerings and the bringing of first-fruits to the Temple, viz. (Numbers 28:26)], and the festival of the ingathering [Succoth] at the going out of the year, when you gather your labor from the field [against the rain].

Three times a year, every male among you must appear before the Presence of the Master, Adonoy.

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The first of the first-fruits of your land [even in the sabbatical year] you shall bring to the house of the L-rd your G-d. You shall not cook a kid [any young, tender animal] in its mother's milk. Do not bow down to their gods and do not worship them and do not emulate their deeds, but raze them [their idols] and break down their [stone] monuments [which they set up to bow down to].


###### Exodus 23:25

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:25](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:25)

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You must serve Adonoy, your God, and He will bless your bread and your water. I will eliminate sickness from your midst.

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall serve the L-rd your G-d, and He will bless your bread and your water, and I shall remove sickness from your midst.


###### Exodus 23:26

###### Exodus 23:27

###### Exodus 23:28

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:28](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:28)

###### Exodus 23:29

I will not drive them out in a single year, lest the land become desolate, and the beasts of the field multiply against you.

I will not drive them out from before thee in one year; lest the land become desolate, and the wild beasts multiply against thee.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

## Chapter 24

###### Exodus 24:1

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
He [God] had said to Moshe, ‘Go up to [the Presence of] Adonoy, you, Aharon, Nadav, Avihu, and seventy of the elders of [the B’nei] Yisrael, and prostrate yourselves at a distance.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And he said to Moshe, Come up to the Lord, thou, and Aharon, Nadav, and Avihu, and seventy of the elders of Yisra᾽el; and bow down afar off.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

###### Exodus 24:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/24:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/24:2)


וְנִגַּ֨שׁ מֹשֶׁ֤ה לְבַדּוֹ֙ אֶל־יְהֹוָ֔ה וְהֵ֖ם לֹ֣א יִגָּ֑שׁוּ וְהָעָ֕ם לֹ֥א יַעֲל֖וּ עִמּֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Moshe alone shall approach [the Presence of] Adonoy, but they must not approach, and the people must not go up with him.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And Moshe alone shall come near the Lord: but they shall not come near; nor shall the people go up with him.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Moses alone shall draw near [to the mist] to the L-rd, but they shall not draw near, and the people shall not go up with him.


###### Exodus 24:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/24:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/24:3)


וַיָּבֹ֣א מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיְסַפֵּ֤ר לָעָם֙ אֵ֚ת כׇּל־דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֔ה וְאֵ֖ת כׇּל־הַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֑ים וַיַּ֨עַן כׇּל־הָעָ֜ם ק֤וֹל אֶחָד֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ כׇּל־הַדְּבָרִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהֹוָ֖ה נַעֲשֶֽׂה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Moses came and he told the people [on that day] all the words of the L-rd [the commandment of separation (from conjugal relations) and the keeping of bounds (from Mount Sinai)] and all of the judgments [the seven Noachide laws, Sabbath, honoring of father and mother, and the administration of justice, which had been related to them at Marah]. And the people answered with one voice and said: All of the things which the L-rd has spoken we shall do.

וַיִּכְתֹּ֣ב מֹשֶׁ֗ה אֵ֚ת כׇּל־דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֔ה וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֣ם בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וַיִּ֥בֶן מִזְבֵּ֖חַ תַּ֣חַת הָהָ֑ר וּשְׁתֵּ֤ים עֶשְׂרֵה֙ מַצֵּבָ֔ה לִשְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ר שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

###### Exodus 24:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/24:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/24:8)

וַיִּרְא֕וּ אֵ֖ת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְתַ֣חַת רַגְלָ֗יו כְּמַעֲשֵׂה֙ לִבְנַ֣ת הַסַּפִּ֔יר וּכְעֶ֥צֶם הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם לָטֹֽהַר׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

[When they were redeemed, there was light and rejoicing before Him.]

###### Exodus 24:12

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The glory of Adonoy rested on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days. On the seventh day, He called to Moshe from the midst of the cloud.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the glory of the Lord rested upon mount Sinay, and the cloud covered it for six days: on the seventh day he called to Moshe out of the midst of the cloud.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the glory of the L-rd reposed upon Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days and He called to Moses on the seventh day from the midst of the cloud. [Or, according to another view, him. ("it"): "And the glory of the L-rd reposed upon Mount Sinai and the cloud covered it for six days [from Rosh Chodesh Sivan], and He called to Moses [(all of Israel standing there, but Moses being singled out for special honor)] on the seventh day [to declare the Ten Commandments] from the midst of the cloud." ("him"): "And the glory of the L-rd reposed upon Mount Sinai and the cloud covered him for six days [after the Ten Commandments, the beginning of the forty days of Moses' going up to receive the tablets (Scripture teaching that entrance into the "Divine Encampment" (later, the Holy of Holies) requires a six-day separation period)], and He called to Moses on the seventh day from the midst of the cloud."]

דַּבֵּר֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְיִקְחוּ־לִ֖י תְּרוּמָ֑ה מֵאֵ֤ת כׇּל־אִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִדְּבֶ֣נּוּ לִבּ֔וֹ תִּקְח֖וּ אֶת־תְּרוּמָתִֽי׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Speak to the B’nei Yisrael and have them take for Me a terumah-offering. From every man whose heart impels him to generosity shall you take My terumah-offering.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Speak to the children of Yisra᾽el that they bring me an offering: of every man whose heart prompts him to give you shall take my offering.

[Three terumoth are referred to here: the terumah of a beka for a head, of which the sockets were made; the terumah of the altar, a beka for a head, for the communal offering funds; and the terumah of the mishkan (the tabernacle), an individual gift. (The thirteen articles mentioned below were needed either for the work of the mishkan or for the priestly garments)].

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And see, and make (them) according to their design which you are shown [here] in the mountain.

###### Exodus 26:1
